signals.title: fix(profiles): find alias collisions without shelling out to where
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? `check_alias_collision()` shells out to `where` (Windows) / `which` (POSIX) and compares the decoded first line against a path it builds itself: ```python result = subprocess.run( ["where" if is_windows else "which", canon], capture_output=True, text=True, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace', timeout=5, ) existing_path = result.stdout.strip().splitlines()[0] expected = wrapper_dir / (f"{canon}.bat" if is_windows else canon) if existing_path == str(expected): ... # our own wrapper, safe to overwrite return f"'{canon}' conflicts with an existing command ({existing_path})" ``` `expected` comes from the filesystem and is correct. `existing_path` comes from a native console program decoded as UTF-8. `where.exe` writes the machine code page, so on a CJK host the two can never be compared meaningfully. `_get_wrapper_dir()` is `Path.home() / ".local" / "bin"`, so the wrapper path contains the user profile name. An account named in kana or kanji puts non-ASCII on both sides of that comparison. **Measured on ja-JP Windows 11 (ACP=932), Python 3.12.10.** A directory named 十能予 on PATH, holding `hermesprobe.bat`, then the same `where` call captured as bytes: ``` raw bytes 27 raw hex 43 3a 5c 8f 5c 94 5c 97 5c 5c 6865726d657370726f62652e626174 0d 0a C : \ 十 能 予 \ hermesprobe.bat CRLF cp932 'C:\\\u5341\u80fd\u4e88\\hermesprobe.bat\r\n' utf-8 + replace 'C:\\\ufffd\\\ufffd\\\ufffd\\\\hermesprobe.bat\r\n' backslashes expected 2 cp932 2 utf-8 5 match cp932 True match utf8 False ``` This is not the usual replacement-character story. All three characters have `0x5C` as their CP932 trail byte, and `0x5C` is the path separator, so the decode does not lose the path — it **adds three separators to it**. There are 52 such characters in CPython's CP932 double-byte table and they are ordinary ones: 表 十 能 予 構 貼. **What it costs.** `check_alias_collision` is called from eight places (`main.py` ×3, `web_routers/profiles.py` ×2, `cli_commands_mixin.py`, `backup.py` ×2), including profile import and backup restore. With the comparison unable to hold, the "this is our own wrapper, safe to overwrite" branch is unreachable, so re-creating an alias you already own fails with: ``` 'hermesprobe' conflicts with an existing command (C:\<?>\<?>\<?>\\hermesprobe.bat) ``` `errors='replace'` means nothing raises, so this surfaces only as that message. **The fix.** `shutil.which()` instead of the subprocess. It reads `PATH` and `PATHEXT` in-process and returns the first match — the same value `.splitlines()[0]` was taking — so no byte boundary exists to get the codepage wrong. `shutil` was already imported. The net change removes a spawn, a 5-second timeout, and two exception arms. One behaviour difference this introduces and then closes: `shutil.which` joins onto the PATH entry verbatim, so a Windows `PATH` carrying `C:/tools` yields `C:/tools\mybot.bat`, where `where` normalised the separator. `os.path.normcase` on both sides folds separator and case on Windows and is a no-op on POSIX. **The alternative I did not take.** Keeping the subprocess and passing `encoding=locale.getencoding()` is a one-line diff and matches #89907 / #90017. I preferred deleting the boundary: this lookup never needed a child process, `check-windows-footguns.py` already lists `shutil.which(` among its guard hints, and the diff comes out smaller. Happy to switch to the minimal form if you would rather keep the change surface at one line. ## Related Issue No separate issue — reporting it here with the measurement. Same family as #89878 / #89907 / #90017 / #90046, but this site does not merely mangle text for display: the corrupted string is an operand in an equality test against a correct path. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `hermes_cli/profiles.py` — `check_alias_collision()` resolves PATH with `shutil.which()` instead of `subprocess.run(["where"|"which", ...])`, and compares through `os.path.normcase`. - `tests/hermes_cli/test_profiles.py` — `test_windows_checks_bat_extension` and `test_traversal_alias_rejected_before_path_lookup` now patch `shutil.which` rather than `subprocess.run`. - `tests/hermes_cli/test_profiles.py` — four tests added: no child process is spawned for the lookup; a wrapper under a non-ASCII directory is recognised through a real PATH lookup; a PATH entry written with forward slashes still matches; and a byte-level assertion pinning what CP932 does under a UTF-8 decode. ## How to Test 1. On a CP932 host, reproduce the decode against the same call: ```powershell mkdir C:\十能予 -Force "@echo off" | Out-File -Encoding ascii C:\十能予\hermesprobe.bat $env:PATH = "C:\十能予;$env:PATH" ``` ```python import subprocess raw = subprocess.run(["where", "hermesprobe"], capture_output=True).stdout print(raw.hex()) print(ascii(raw.decode("cp932"))) print(ascii(raw.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))) ``` The backslash count goes from 2 to 5. Output above is from that run. 2. `python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_profiles.py -q` on that same host, against `upstream/main` and against this branch: ``` upstream/main 8 failed, 48 passed this branch 8 failed, 52 passed ``` The same eight fail on both, and none of them are in `TestAliasCollision`. They are pre-existing Windows failures in this file, four distinct causes: - two `assert 438 == 384` — a byte count that assumes LF line endings - two asserting a POSIX wrapper name against the `.bat` one Windows actually writes (`assert 'mybot.bat' == 'mybot'`) - two needing the symlink privilege (`OSError: [WinError 1314]`) - two `Path.read_text()` without `encoding=` raising `UnicodeDecodeError: 'cp932' codec can't decode byte 0x94` inside the test file itself The four extra passes are the four tests this PR adds. 3. Against the pre-patch source with the new tests kept, `-k AliasCollision` gives 1 failed / 4 passed. Only `test_path_lookup_does_not_spawn_a_child_process` is a genuine regression test off Windows — the others cannot fail on a UTF-8 host because there is no decode to get wrong there, and I would rather say that than imply four-way coverage. `test_wrapper_recognised_when_its_path_is_not_ascii` does a real PATH lookup with nothing mocked, so it is a real regression test on native Windows and a no-op assertion elsewhere. That pre-patch comparison was run in a Linux checkout of the same commit, not on the Windows host. Note on the checklist below: I ran `tests/hermes_cli/test_profiles.py` and the before/after comparison above, not the full `pytest tests/ -q`, so I left that box unchecked rather than claiming it. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11, ja-JP (ACP=932), Python 3.12.10 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A ## Screenshots / Logs I have a ja-JP (ACP=932) Windows host and can measure anything else on that locale. *(Measured on my host. Drafted with Claude.)*

signals.title: fix(desktop): stop decoding the HERMES_HOME registry read as utf-8
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? `readWindowsUserEnvVar()` reads `HERMES_HOME` out of `HKCU\Environment` and decodes `reg.exe`'s stdout as UTF-8: ```ts stdout = exec('reg', ['query', 'HKCU\\Environment', '/v', name], { encoding: 'utf8', windowsHide: true, timeout: 5000 }) ``` `reg.exe` is a native console program; its stdout carries the machine code page. The value being read is a filesystem path. **Measured on ja-JP Windows 11 (ACP=932), Node v24.17.0.** `setx HERMES_PROBE "C:\十能予\hermes"`, then the same `reg query` captured as bytes: ``` raw bytes 83 value hex 43 3a 5c 8f 5c 94 5c 97 5c 5c 6865726d6573 C : \ 十 能 予 \ hermes parsed, utf8 "C:\\\ufffd\\\ufffd\\\ufffd\\\\hermes" parsed, sjis "C:\\\u5341\u80fd\u4e88\\hermes" backslashes utf8 5 sjis 2 values equal false parent exists, utf8 false parent exists, sjis true ``` The three characters each have `0x5C` as their CP932 trail byte, and `0x5C` is the path separator. So the UTF-8 decode does not shorten the path, it **lengthens** it by three segments. There are 52 such characters in CPython's CP932 double-byte table, and they are ordinary ones: 表 十 能 予 構 貼. **What it costs.** `parseRegQueryValue` matches on `\S+` for the name and takes the rest of the line as the value, so a mangled value parses cleanly. The caller in `main.ts` is: ```ts const fromRegistry = readWindowsUserEnvVar('HERMES_HOME') if (fromRegistry) { return normalizeHermesHomeRoot(fromRegistry) } // LOCALAPPDATA fallback below is never reached ``` A corrupted string is still truthy, so the desktop resolves `HERMES_HOME` to a directory that does not exist rather than falling through to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`. That is worse than the stale-snapshot gap this function was added to close (#45471): the fallback that would have produced a working home is skipped by a value that only looks valid. `parent exists utf8 = false` above is that outcome on a real host. **The fix.** Node exposes no API for the host ANSI or OEM code page, so rather than guess at one: - Take `reg`'s stdout as bytes (drop `encoding: 'utf8'`). - If every byte is `< 0x80`, the code page and UTF-8 agree by definition — decode and return, unchanged behaviour and no extra spawn. This is the path essentially every host takes. - If any byte is `>= 0x80`, the value is in a code page we cannot name. Re-read it through PowerShell base64-encoded from UTF-8 inside the child, so the bytes on the wire are ASCII and no code page is involved: ``` [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes( [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('HERMES_HOME','User'))) ``` That is the same trick `ui-tui/src/lib/clipboard.ts` and `hermes_cli/clipboard.py` already use for clipboard text, for the same reason. The trigger is a fact about the bytes, not a judgement about damage. I deliberately did not detect this by looking for `U+FFFD`: I measured on #89468 that the replacement output is not stable across runtimes (29 replacements on .NET Framework 4.8, 30 on .NET 8 and CPython 3.11 for identical input), so replacement characters are not a sound signal. The name is checked against `/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/` before it is interpolated into the PowerShell string. Today the only caller passes a literal, but the function is exported. **Note on the linter.** `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py` cannot see this file: `should_scan_file()` returns `True` only for `.py`, `.pyw`, `.pyi`. Every `.ts` under `apps/desktop/electron/` is outside the gate that exists to catch exactly this class of bug. ## Related Issue No separate issue — reporting it here with the measurement. Same class as #89878 / #89907 / #90017 / #90046, on the Electron side of the same seam. The Python half of `bounded_probe_run` is #90046; this is the TypeScript half, and it is independent of that PR. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `apps/desktop/electron/windows-user-env.ts` — added `isAsciiBytes()`; `readWindowsUserEnvVar()` now captures `reg` stdout as bytes and only decodes it as UTF-8 when it is pure ASCII. - `apps/desktop/electron/windows-user-env.ts` — added `readUserEnvVarAsBase64()`, a PowerShell re-read that base64-encodes the UTF-8 bytes inside the child, used only on the non-ASCII path. Env-var names are validated before interpolation. - `apps/desktop/electron/windows-user-env.test.ts` — four tests added: the ASCII fast path spawns only `reg`; a CP932 value is re-read as base64 and returns the correct path, with the old five-backslash result pinned as an assertion; a failed re-read returns `null`; a name that is not a plain identifier never reaches PowerShell. ## How to Test 1. On a CP932 host: ```powershell mkdir C:\十能予 -Force setx HERMES_PROBE "C:\十能予\hermes" ``` Then, in a new shell: ```js const { execFileSync } = require('node:child_process') const raw = execFileSync('reg', ['query','HKCU\\Environment','/v','HERMES_PROBE'], { windowsHide: true }) console.log(raw.toString('hex')) console.log(JSON.stringify(raw.toString('utf8'))) console.log(JSON.stringify(new TextDecoder('shift_jis').decode(raw))) ``` The backslash count goes from 2 to 5, and `fs.statSync` on the parent of the UTF-8 result throws. Output above is from that run. 2. The test file, run directly under `node --test` with the type annotations stripped — 14 pass (10 pre-existing, unchanged). I did not run it through the repo's vitest runner: the desktop workspace's dependencies are not installed on my host, so `npm test -w apps/desktop` is not something I can honestly claim to have run. 3. Against the pre-patch source, keeping the new tests: 2 failed / 12 passed. The other two pass either way on purpose — one pins that the ASCII path still spawns only `reg` so the common case cannot regress, the other pins the name-validation guard, which is new but not what the bug was. Note on the checklist below: I left the full-suite box unchecked for the reason in 2. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11, ja-JP (ACP=932), Node v24.17.0 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A ## Screenshots / Logs I have a ja-JP (ACP=932) Windows host and can measure anything else on that locale. *(Measured on my host. Drafted with Claude.)*

signals.title: fix(windows): resolve memory provider command shims
signals.text:
## Summary Fix native-Windows memory-provider dependency checks for CLI tools installed through npm shims such as ByteRover's `brv.cmd`. On Windows, the dashboard and `hermes memory setup` were passing a bare command like `brv` directly to `subprocess.run([...])`. Python ultimately calls `CreateProcessW`, which does not perform PATHEXT resolution for this argv form, so a valid npm-installed CLI could fail with: ```text FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified ``` This caused the Plugins page to report ByteRover as missing even while: ```text where.exe brv C:
vm4w
odejs rv C:
vm4w
odejs rv.cmd brv --version byterover-cli/3.16.1 win32-x64 node-v22.23.2 hermes memory status Plugin: installed Status: available ``` ## Fix - split external dependency check commands with Windows-aware `shlex` behavior - resolve argv[0] with `shutil.which()` on Windows before calling `subprocess.run` - apply the same fix to: - CLI memory-provider setup - dashboard dependency-installed checks - dashboard pre-install checks - dashboard post-install verification - preserve the existing behavior when the executable cannot be resolved For an npm-installed ByteRover CLI this turns: ```text brv --version ``` into an argv beginning with the actual launcher, e.g.: ```text C:
vm4w
odejs rv.CMD ``` ## Regression coverage Adds tests covering: - `.cmd` shim resolution in the dashboard path - unresolved-command fallback behavior - `.cmd` shim resolution in the CLI memory setup path The tests mock Windows behavior so they can run on non-Windows CI as well. ## Reproduction / validation Reproduced on native Windows 11 with NVM for Windows, Node 22.23.2, and `byterover-cli` 3.16.1. Before the fix, the Plugins page returned `missing brv` / `[WinError 2]`; after resolving the shim path and restarting the dashboard, ByteRover showed `ready` and `active` and the dependency warning disappeared. This PR is intentionally scoped to executable resolution. The ByteRover manifest's Unix-oriented install command is a separate portability concern.

signals.title: feat(desktop): Space stages clarify choices from the keyboard
signals.text: ## Summary The desktop clarify card can now be driven fully from the keyboard: **Space stages/toggles the highlighted choice without submitting**, matching the standard option-list convention. Enter stays the confirm key. Inspired by Factory Droid v0.199 ("Question prompt keyboard controls" — answers pickable with Space or number keys). Hermes already had arrow/letter/number navigation on the clarify card; Space was the gap — it did nothing on the card and fell through to the global type-to-focus listener, which yanked focus into the composer with a leading space, silently killing the staged selection. ## Changes - `clarify-tool.tsx`: Space stages the highlighted choice (single-select) or toggles it (multi-select) without submitting; on the "Other" row it focuses the free-text field. - `composer-focus-keys.ts`: a live clarify card now owns the Space key (`clarifyCardOwnsKey`) so type-to-focus yields it — a real composer message never starts with a leading space, so this costs nothing. - Tests: 3 new clarify-tool cases (stage-then-confirm, multi-select toggle, Other-row focus) + updated the composer-focus-keys ownership pin. ## Validation | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Space on highlighted choice | focus jumps to composer, " " typed | choice staged, card keeps focus | | Space on multi-select choice | same composer steal | toggles the choice in the staged set | | `vitest run` clarify-tool + composer-focus-keys | 41 tests | 44/44 pass | Source: [Droid v0.199 release notes](https://docs.factory.ai/changelog/release-notes) (Aug 18, 2026). Their mechanism: Space/number pick answers, Tab moves between questions. Our adaptation: Space maps onto Hermes' existing stage-then-confirm model (Droid picks immediately; we deliberately keep Enter as the explicit confirm, consistent with the card's Continue button). Tab-between-questions was not ported — the batch card stages all questions in one form and native Tab traversal already walks its fields. ## Infographic ![Space stages your choice — keyboard controls for clarify cards](https://files.catbox.moe/70rzd3.png)

signals.title: feat(sdk): add host.preview(url) for plugin-driven preview pane opens
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Add a one-line `host.preview(url)` entry to the desktop plugin SDK so a plugin can surface a URL in the right-rail preview pane — the same UX chat uses for tool-result / file-browser / artifact previews. ## Why? The runtime loader (`contrib/runtime-loader.ts`) restricts disk-loaded plugins to `@hermes/plugin-sdk` and `react`; plugins can't import `@/store/preview` directly. Until now there was no first-class SDK door into the preview store, so plugins had no way to hand the user a server UI, dev tool, or web page without leaving the app (e.g. `window.open` to a system browser, or `target=_blank`). Concrete motivator: the DSH settings plugin (`<hermes home>/desktop-plugins/dsh-settings/`) wants a "Open DSH Web UI" button that pops the DSH chat workspace into the right-rail preview pane — same host, same UX as a tool-result preview. ## How `apps/desktop/src/sdk/index.ts` — add `host.preview(url)`: ```ts import { openPreview } from '@/store/preview' … preview: (url: string) => { if (typeof url !== 'string' || !url.trim()) return openPreview({ kind: 'url', label: url, source: 'plugin', url }, 'manual') } ``` `source: 'plugin'` is a free-form discriminator (the type is `string`) — it's recorded so future telemetry / "close all plugin tabs" affordances can find plugin-opened tabs without conflating them with chat / file-browser / artifact previews. `PreviewRecordSource` (`'manual'` here) is the second arg to `openPreview` and only affects HTML file rendering — for URL targets the rendering path is identical to any other `kind: 'url'` target. The `sdkImportMap` in `src/sdk/runtime.ts` re-exports every named export of `./index` as a shim blob, so the new method is automatically available to runtime-loaded disk plugins with zero loader changes. ## Type of Change - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) ## How to Test 1. Open the desktop app, install a disk plugin that calls `host.preview('https://example.com')` (e.g. a debug plugin). 3. Click the button. 4. Right rail focuses the new preview tab showing example.com — same UX as the chat preview on a tool-result. 5. With a file target (e.g. `/tmp/index.html`) loaded via chat preview, verify the new `host.preview` tab is independent (different `source` discriminator, separate tab id). For the DSH settings plugin (the original motivator): once a desktop release with this PR ships, `dsh-settings`'s "Open DSH Web UI" button can be re-pointed from `<a target="_blank">` to `host.preview('http://127.0.0.1:8080/')`. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] Conventional commit message (`feat(sdk): ...`) - [x] Single-file change, no unrelated commits - [x] Diff is +12 lines (1 import + 11 lines incl. doc-comment)

signal.title: [Bug]: Desktop message age ("8m ago") stops advancing without a re-render
signal.text: ### Bug Description Hermes Desktop can leave an assistant message's relative age frozen indefinitely. In one observed session, the message footer still displayed `8m ago` at 18:38:41 even though the persisted assistant message timestamp was 17:09:23. The actual elapsed time was 1 hour 29 minutes, and `hermes sessions list` correctly reported the session as `1h ago`. The underlying timestamp is correct. Only the rendered relative-age label is stale. This can mislead the operator about whether a response or background activity happened recently. Suggested priority: P3. This is a UI correctness issue with a simple workaround and no observed data loss. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Open a completed chat in Hermes Desktop. 2. Hover an assistant response so its action bar displays a relative age such as `8m ago`. 3. Leave the same chat open long enough to cross one or more minute/hour boundaries, without switching sessions or otherwise triggering a React re-render. 4. Hover or continue hovering the response again. 5. Observe that the label can remain at its old value. 6. Switch to another chat and back, or reload Desktop. 7. Observe that the age is recalculated. ### Expected Behavior The visible relative age should advance as time passes, for example: - `8m ago` → `9m ago` - `59m ago` → `1h ago` It should not require unrelated UI state changes, session navigation, or a reload. ### Actual Behavior The label samples the current time during a render and can then remain frozen until an unrelated render occurs. Observed evidence: - Persisted assistant timestamp: `2026-07-30 17:09:23 +02:00` - Screenshot capture time: `2026-07-30 18:38:41 +02:00` - Displayed label: `8m ago` - Actual elapsed time: approximately 1h 29m - Native CLI session age: `1h ago` ### Affected Component Other — Hermes Desktop, in-thread assistant message footer (`MessageAge`). ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) Not applicable — Desktop UI. ### Debug Report ```shell Not uploaded: this is a deterministic renderer-state bug with no crash, traceback, or relevant log signature. Sanitized local checks confirmed that the persisted timestamp and CLI-derived age were correct; only the Desktop label was stale. ``` ### Operating System Windows 11 Pro, version 10.0.26200, build 26200, 64-bit. ### Python Version Hermes runtime: Python 3.11.15 Shell `python --version`: Python 3.14.6 ### Hermes Version Observed on Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20). The installed runtime reports that it is behind current upstream. However, the same causal code path was inspected on the current `main` branch on 2026-07-30 and is still present there. ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell No error or crash was emitted. The stored session data contains the correct timestamp. ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) On current `main`, `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread/assistant-message.tsx` implements `MessageAge` by: 1. subscribing only to `s.message.createdAt`, which is stable after message creation; and 2. calling `formatAgo(date.getTime(), t.agents)` directly during render. `formatAgo` defaults its `nowMs` argument to `Date.now()`, but `MessageAge` has no reactive clock, interval, scheduled invalidation, or changing state. Consequently, `Date.now()` is sampled only when React happens to render the component. CSS hover visibility does not itself cause another React render. Current code: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread/assistant-message.tsx#L296-L312 This was also confirmed in the packaged Windows bundle used during the incident. ### Proposed Fix (optional) Make the displayed age depend on a reactive notion of `now`. To avoid creating one permanent timer for every message in a long transcript, prefer either: 1. a shared coarse clock for message-age consumers; or 2. subscribing/scheduling updates only while the age control is visible or focused, with the next update scheduled at the next `coarseElapsed` display boundary. Add a fake-timer regression test demonstrating that the label advances from `8m ago` to `9m ago` and then to `1h ago` without any unrelated state update. ### Workaround Switching away from the chat and back, or reloading Desktop, forces the label to be recalculated. This is containment, not a permanent solution. ### Related Issues and Pull Requests - #70450 is related but not a duplicate. It concerns making exact timestamps discoverable through reliable tooltips: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/70450 - #70487 implements those tooltip and accessibility changes, but its `MessageAge` replacement still calculates `formatAgo()` only during render and does not introduce a reactive clock: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/70487 The affected surface overlaps, but the trigger, causal mechanism, acceptance criteria, and required fix are different.

signal.title: Desktop: BOTS roster preview sticks to a stale finished session despite correct backend (app-side index + touch-on-open)
signal.text: ## Summary In the BOTS section of the Hermes desktop sidebar, the preview row for some profiles shows an old, finished session, and clicking the row opens that old session — even though the active/newest sessions exist in the profile's `state.db` and the backend (`profiles.list`, `last_session` / `list_sessions_rich(order_by_last_active=True)`) returns them in the correct order. After a full app restart and clearing the Electron Local Storage the pane briefly shows the correct previews, but the stale state reproduces on the next roster fetch / after opening a row. ## Environment - macOS 26.x (Apple Silicon) - Hermes Desktop (Electron) — agent core v0.20.4 (2026.8.18), containing `8484786` (BOTS roster preview align) and `7dd945b9` (dedupe + canonical chats) - Multiple profiles (default + 7 named), mixture of desktop sessions and CLI sessions (`hermes -p <name> chat -q`) - Bot Mode / Bots pane active (default plugin) ## Steps to reproduce (observed) 1. Use several profiles. Keep a long-running session in profile A (e.g. default). Create sessions in profiles B/C only via CLI (`hermes -p B chat -q ...`), so the newest data in those `state.dbs` comes from outside the app. 2. Open the BOTS pane. Some rows correctly show the newest session; others (here: default, seth, mac-admin) show a **finished, older session** (in our case: a 2-day-old hidden session, a previous-day session, and a 3-week-old session) although newer sessions exist in those `state.dbs`. 3. Clicking such a row opens the displayed stale session instead of the active one (the symptom of #88200, which is supposed to be fixed by PR #88690). 4. Fully quit the app, clear `~/Library/Application Support/Hermes/Local Storage/leveldb/`, restart: the pane briefly shows the correct previews, then the stale state returns after further interaction / roster refresh. ## Diagnostic data - **Backend is correct:** direct `SessionDB.list_sessions_rich(source=None, limit=20, order_by_last_active=True, compact_rows=True)` returns the active/newest session first for all affected profiles. - **Touch-on-open:** opening/viewing a session updates `sessions.last_activity_at` with provenance `unknown` and an empty description (no chat-activity code). A mac-admin session from 2026-07-31 received such an update on 2026-08-19 16:17 after a stray command — a 3-week-old session became "most recently active" again. This is a self-fulfilling loop: the pane shows the stale row → opening/touching it renews its activity → it stays "last session". - **App-side index:** `hermes.desktop.sessionSeenCounts`, `hermes.desktop.lastSessionId(.profile.<name>)`, `hermes.desktop.sessionOrder`, `hermes.desktop.sessionTiles.v2` in the Electron Local Storage are rebuilt from UI interactions after a storage reset — the Local Storage is the only app-side persistence (Session Storage / Partitions / SharedStorage contain no `hermes.desktop` markers). - **hidden sessions are not filtered** when the roster preview is chosen: a hidden (`hidden=1`) session from 2026-08-17 was shown as the default profile's preview while the pinned active session was newer. ## Expected behavior - The BOTS row preview and the session opened on click describe the same, most relevant (non-archived, non-hidden) session — ideally sourced from the backend's `last_session`/`preferred_session` resolution. - Viewing/opening a session (touch) should not count as conversation activity for roster ordering (or should use a separate "viewed" field that does not displace `last_activity_at`). ## Suggested fix direction 1. Skip `archived`/`hidden` sessions when selecting the roster preview (`_latest_profile_session_row`). 2. Do not let preview/open interactions write `last_activity_at` without provenance (separate touch/view field, or provenance check). 3. Prefer the backend-computed `last_session` over the app-local index when they diverge (single source of truth for roster ordering). ## Workaround (used locally) - Mark ghost sessions `archived=1` in their profile `state.db` (data preserved), fully quit the app, clear Local Storage leveldb, restart. The pane then stays on the active sessions. Requires a manual DB edit — not user-friendly. ## Related - #88200 (BOTS sidebar preview shows wrong session content on click — closed via #88690; covers the pin/preferred path only) - #88340 (duplicate roster identities), #88341 (dedupe + canonical chats), #88690 (pinned canonical Bot Chat salvage) - #88918 (canonical Bot Chat stuck on 429), #89556 (re-opening focused session from Bots panel hangs), #89834 (clicking bot after group chat does not show the bot's chat)
signal.author: HORUS-71

signal.title: [Enhancement] Structured per-run execution context for /v1/runs: task metadata, cwd, and policy-bounded execution options
signal.text: **Version:** hermes-agent 0.20.3 ## Summary `POST /v1/runs` accepts `input`, `instructions`, `session_id`, `conversation_history`, `previous_response_id` and a model route. Anything else a caller needs to vary *per run* has no field to travel in, so it must either be flattened into the prompt or pinned lane-wide in `config.yaml`. That forces a one-lane-per-posture deployment model: every group of runs that differs in working directory, toolset, or turn budget needs its own gateway process, its own `HERMES_HOME`, and its own port. For an orchestrator driving a handful of differently-configured agents, most of the operational benefit of a shared worker disappears. Three related gaps, filed together because they all stem from the same missing abstraction. ## The governing invariant Stated first because it should shape the design rather than be bolted on: > **A client may restrict the capabilities already granted to a gateway lane, but may never widen them.** And: **prefer explicit rejection over silent narrowing.** If a lane permits `[terminal, file]` and a run requests `[terminal, file, browser]`, the request should be rejected — not silently reduced to `[terminal, file]`. Silent narrowing means a caller cannot distinguish "applied" from "ignored", which is how a run quietly does less than the operator's automation believes it did. This applies uniformly to every field below: cwd roots, toolsets, numeric limits, model routes, approval posture. The property to preserve is that holding an `API_SERVER_KEY` grants no authority the operator did not already grant the lane. ## 3a — Run/task/wake metadata There is no structured channel for caller-side correlation identifiers. A client can push them into the prompt (and today's clients do), but nothing the *tools* run by the agent can read, and nothing that lets agent-side logs be correlated to an orchestrator run without parsing free text. `Idempotency-Key` carries a correlation id on the wire but reaches nothing inside the run. **Ask:** a `context` object on run creation, exposed to the run as environment variables under a reserved prefix: ```json {"context": {"run_id": "…", "task_id": "…", "wake_reason": "…", "payload": {...}}} ``` Non-secret by definition — anything sensitive belongs in the separate secrets channel (#90438), not here. ## 3b — Working directory and workspace Every run on a lane inherits that lane's single `terminal.cwd`. Concurrent runs therefore share a working directory and can collide on files, and a run that needs a specific checkout cannot be expressed without standing up a dedicated lane. **Ask:** `cwd`, and optionally `worktree`, on run creation. **Bounded by:** an operator-configured allowlist of permitted roots. A `cwd` outside the allowlist is rejected with a clear error, never clamped to the lane default — silently running in the wrong directory is worse than failing. ## 3c — Constrained execution options Toolsets, max turns, checkpoints and reasoning effort are all lane-wide today. Toolsets come from `platform_toolsets.api_server`; turn limits and checkpoints from `config.yaml`. **Ask:** an `options` object on run creation covering at least toolsets, max turns, checkpoints and reasoning effort. **Bounded by:** - `options.toolsets` must be a **subset** of the lane's configured toolsets. A name the lane does not permit is a rejection, not a silent drop. - Numeric limits capped at the lane's configured maximum; a request above the cap is rejected. - If approval mode ever becomes per-run, it may only tighten relative to the lane setting, never loosen it. ## Related: a route-conflict rough edge Adjacent and cheap to fix alongside this. `_handle_runs` calls `_request_route_conflict_error(...)`, which rejects a request that supplies `model`/`provider` together with a `session_id`. Since a client using session continuity always sends `session_id`, the one per-run override that *is* supported is unusable in that mode — the request comes back as a route conflict rather than as a clear statement of the rule. Either allow `model` alongside `session_id` when the session is new, or return an error that names the constraint explicitly. ## Related issues - #90438 — run-scoped secret delivery. Deliberately **not** part of this proposal: credential handling is a different security boundary and should not share a design review with per-run ergonomics. - #2971 — structured run events and resumable clarify/approval interactions. - paperclipai/paperclip#7899 — the same per-run env expectation, unmet in a different adapter, which suggests the gap is not specific to one client. ## Context Found while evaluating the Hermes API server as an execution backend for an orchestrator that currently shells out to `hermes chat` locally. The local CLI expresses all of the above per invocation (`--in`, `-t`, `--max-turns`, `--checkpoints`, plus process environment); the API server expresses none of it per run. Closing that gap is what would make the API server a drop-in replacement for the CLI path rather than a differently-shaped one.

signal.title: [Bug]: Running kanban/tool workers are invisible in Desktop UI (session list filters them; Bots ACTIVE NOW ignores worker activity)
signal.text: ### Bug Description Long-running kanban worker runs (`hermes -p <profile> ... chat -q work kanban task <id>` spawned by the dispatcher) are completely invisible in the Desktop UI while they run: 1. **Session list:** worker sessions never appear in the SESSIONS sidebar. `tui_gateway/methods_session.py` hard-codes `deny = frozenset({"kanban", "tool"})` when building the session list, with no config override. For workers that run 10–30 minutes (coding tasks with test suites), the user sees no evidence that anything is running. 2. **Bots tab / ACTIVE NOW:** the per-bot "last active" timestamp and the ACTIVE NOW row only reflect bot **chat** activity (DMs / group acks). A profile whose kanban worker is actively running for 12+ minutes still shows "3 hr ago", and ACTIVE NOW lists only the chief. Verified concurrently: `ps` shows the worker process alive and mid-run while the Bots tab shows the profile as idle. Together this makes Bot Mode feel unresponsive/dead during exactly the moments it is doing its heaviest work — the user's only recourse is `hermes kanban list` in a terminal. Setup: Bot Mode v2 with 6 specialist profiles + default chief; Desktop (macOS) connected via **Remote gateway** to a central `hermes serve` on a Linux VPS (loopback + SSH tunnel); kanban dispatcher embedded in gateway. Possibly related (neighboring areas, none tracks this gap itself): #89756, #88897, #77829. _Report compiled with agent assistance; both symptoms verified live on our deployment._ ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Bot Mode v2 with at least one specialist profile; kanban dispatcher running. 2. Create a kanban task assigned to that profile with a long-running body (e.g. a code change with tests), let the dispatcher spawn the worker. 3. While the worker runs: SESSIONS sidebar shows no session for it; Bots tab shows the profile's last chat time (stale) and no ACTIVE NOW entry. ### Expected Behavior - Sessions sidebar: worker sessions with a live agent should be listable (ideally behind a config flag, e.g. `sessions.show_active_workers`, shown as their own group analogous to TELEGRAM/CRON JOBS, and hidden again once finished so the list is not flooded). - Bots tab: a profile should count as active (ACTIVE NOW + fresh "last active", possibly tagged "kanban") while a kanban/tool worker is running under that profile, falling back to the last chat timestamp when the worker ends. - Note: the second `deny` use in `methods_session.py` (TUI auto-resume) should probably keep excluding workers — auto-resume onto a worker session would be wrong; only the list surface needs the override. ### Actual Behavior While a kanban worker is running (verified via `ps`: `hermes -p coding ... chat -q work kanban task <id>` alive 12+ minutes): - SESSIONS sidebar shows no session entry for the worker. - Bots tab shows the worker's profile with a stale timestamp ("3 hr ago", from its last chat), and ACTIVE NOW lists only the chief profile. - No error output — the work completes fine; it is purely a visibility gap. The only way to see the running work is `hermes kanban list` in a terminal. ### Affected Component Other ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) _No response_ ### Debug Report ```shell Not attaching the automated debug-share upload (contains org config/log details we prefer not to publish). Key evidence inline instead: - `tui_gateway/methods_session.py` (v0.20.4): `deny = frozenset({"kanban", "tool"})` in the session-list builder (and a second, correct use in TUI auto-resume). - Observed 2026-08-19 ~22:35 CEST: `ps` shows `hermes -p coding ... chat -q work kanban task <id>` alive for 12+ min while Bots tab shows "Coding · 3 hr ago" and ACTIVE NOW lists only the chief; SESSIONS sidebar shows no entry for the worker session. Happy to provide targeted log excerpts on request. ``` ### Operating System Backend: Debian-based Linux VPS (kernel 6.x); Desktop client: macOS 15 (Darwin 25.5) ### Python Version 3.11.15 ### Hermes Version v0.20.4 (2026.8.18) ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) _No response_ ### Proposed Fix (optional) _No response_ ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

signal.title: fix(bot-mode): prevent ordinary sessions from being hidden
signal.text: ## Summary Fix a Bot Mode session-ownership bug that can hide ordinary desktop conversations from the global Sessions sidebar. ## Problem When a Bot profile had no canonical `Bot Chat` pointer, Bot Mode adopted the profile's latest session based only on recency. If that latest session was an ordinary user conversation, its ID was persisted as `hermes-bots.chat`. The startup reconciliation sweep then treated the ID as Bot Mode-owned and set `hidden=true`. This caused unrelated project conversations to disappear from the desktop session list while remaining present in `state.db`. ## Changes - Only adopt or recover previewed sessions whose durable root title is `Bot Chat`. - Expose `root_title` in the precise `profiles.list` preferred-session summary so compressed canonical chats remain valid even when the live tip is titled `Bot Chat (continued)` or otherwise differs from the root. - Reject a pinned session if the backend resolves it to an ordinary conversation; clear the corrupt pointer and create a fresh Bot Chat. - Validate canonical pointers through `profiles.list` before issuing `session.set_hidden`. - Fail closed when validation is unavailable: an old Bot Chat may remain visible, but an ordinary session is never hidden. - Add regression coverage for ordinary latest sessions, stale pins, stale hide-sweep pointers, and compressed canonical chats. ## Verification - `npm run check:test:plugins` — 312/312 tests passed. - Targeted canonical/hide tests — passed after the final change. - Regression sabotage check: the new safety tests fail with the pre-fix implementation. - `npm run pack` completed successfully for macOS arm64 before the root-title compatibility refinement. - The targeted backend pytest was not runnable locally because the repository virtual environments do not include pytest; CI should execute it. ## Scope This change does not alter the intended behavior for actual Bot Mode plumbing sessions (`Bot Chat`, `Agent Inbox`, and `Group: ...`). It does not include unrelated working-tree files.

signal.title: fix(bot-mode): hide sweep and chat adoption can no longer swallow ordinary sessions (salvage #89901)
signal.text: ## Summary Bot Mode's hide sweep and canonical-chat adoption can no longer claim or hide a user's ordinary conversation — every hide/adopt/re-anchor path now verifies the target is actual Bot Mode plumbing (title "Bot Chat", or root title across compression) and fails closed. Salvages PR #89901 by @Owen-narcissus onto current main with authorship preserved (clean cherry-pick, zero conflicts against the merged #90326 activity work). ## Changes - `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js`: - `hideOwnedBotSessions()` resolves every stored canonical pointer through `profiles.list` `preferred_session_ids` and requires the "Bot Chat" title before `session.set_hidden` — a stale pointer at an ordinary session is never hidden (fail-closed on old gateways too). - Grandfather/adopt, pin verification, and dead-pin recovery only accept Bot Chat sessions; a pin resolving to an ordinary session is treated as corrupted metadata (cleared + fresh Bot Chat created), never opened-and-hidden. - `tui_gateway/methods_profiles.py`: `preferred_session` gains `root_title` (durable pin's own title) so compression-rotated Bot Chats ("Bot Chat (continued)") still verify. - Tests: 4 new safety tests (stale pointer not hidden; ordinary latest not adopted; pinned ordinary replaced; dead pin doesn't steal ordinary latest) + root_title contract coverage. ## Validation | | Result | |---|---| | `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` (hermes-bots) | 319/319 pass | | `pytest tests/tui_gateway/test_profiles_list_preferred_session.py` | 8/8 pass | | `node --check plugin.js` | clean | ## Infographic ![Ordinary chats are safe](https://files.catbox.moe/9ggwjb.png)

signal.title: /v1/runs has no channel to deliver a run-scoped secret to the run environment — credentials can only travel as model context
signal.text: **Version:** hermes-agent 0.20.3 ## Summary `POST /v1/runs` has no channel for delivering a per-run secret to the run's execution environment. Every field it accepts — `input`, `instructions`, `conversation_history`, `previous_response_id`, `session_id` — is model context: prompted, persisted to the session transcript, and logged. The only credential on the wire today is the caller's own `API_SERVER_KEY`, which authenticates the caller to Hermes and is not usable as the run's identity to a third system. Orchestrators that wake Hermes through the API server need the run to hold a short-lived, run-scoped credential for calling *back* into the orchestrator. Without a secret channel the options are all bad: bake one static credential into the Hermes host environment and lose per-run scoping, or push the token through `input`/`instructions` and put a bearer token into prompts, transcripts and logs. ## Why this is not solvable client-side The natural workaround — putting the token in the run payload — is the thing that must not happen. Concretely, in the Paperclip gateway adapter (paperclipai/paperclip#9956), the run body already carries runtime identity as prompt text: ``` Paperclip runtime identity: - Agent ID: … - Company ID: … - Run ID: … - Paperclip API URL: … ``` along with an instruction to use an API key "when a Paperclip API key is available" — a key that has nowhere to arrive from. If that gap is closed by threading the token through the same payload surface, the 401s stop and a run-scoped bearer token starts landing in model context instead. That is a worse outcome than the bug. ## Ask A dedicated write-only field on run creation, e.g.: ```json POST /v1/runs { "input": "…", "instructions": "…", "secrets": { "PAPERCLIP_API_KEY": "<run-scoped token>" } } ``` with these properties: 1. **Injected into the run's process environment**, not into the prompt, system prompt, or conversation history. 2. **Never persisted** to the session transcript or state store. 3. **Never echoed** — absent from `GET /v1/runs/{id}`, from every SSE frame on `/v1/runs/{id}/events` including error and status events, and from server logs at any level. The server should redact on the way in rather than relying on callers to avoid reading it back. 4. **Run-scoped lifetime** — dropped when the run terminates, not inherited by a later run that resumes the same `session_id`. 5. **Bounded by operator policy** — an allowlist of injectable variable names in gateway config, so an API-key holder cannot set arbitrary environment variables (e.g. `PATH`, `LD_PRELOAD`) in the Hermes host process. Names outside the allowlist should be rejected explicitly rather than silently dropped. Point 5 matters as much as the others: an unrestricted env-injection field would be a privilege-escalation surface, turning "can create runs" into "can influence how the host executes them". ## Related - paperclipai/paperclip#9956 — the downstream symptom: every orchestrator callback from a gateway-executed agent returns 401, because no channel delivers the run-scoped credential. - #2971 — structured run events and resumable interactions on the API server (adjacent surface, distinct ask). Filed separately from the per-run execution-context proposal because this one is a credential-handling boundary rather than an ergonomics gap, and the two should not share a design review.
signal.author: dialthewolff

signal.title: fix(bot-mode): a running kanban/tool worker now lights its bot's roster row (#90268)
signal.text: ## Summary A profile running a long kanban/tool worker now reads as active in the Desktop Bots roster (ACTIVE NOW entry, pulse dot, fresh age) instead of idling at "3 hr ago" for the whole run (#90268). Root cause: worker sessions are deny-listed out of every conversation list (correctly — auto-resume and shared lists must not see them), so no roster surface ever saw worker activity. Workers DO heartbeat `last_activity_at` every ≤60s while running (#72016) — the signal existed, it just wasn't reported. ## Changes - `tui_gateway/methods_profiles.py`: `profiles.list` rows gain `worker_session` — the newest kanban/tool row (id, source, title, last_active) from the same single listing pass. `last_session` keeps its deny-list contract; `include_sessions: false` omits the field; older clients ignore it. - `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js`: `workerActiveAt()` (150s window — one missed heartbeat of slack) feeds ACTIVE NOW, the row pulse dot (tooltip "Working on a task right now"), and the row age label while the worker runs. Chat behavior unchanged when no worker is live; falls back to last chat timestamp when the worker ends. - Session-list visibility of workers (the issue's other half) intentionally unchanged — surfacing workers in shared lists would break auto-resume and flood the sidebar; the roster signal was the actionable gap. ## Validation | | Result | |---|---| | `pytest tests/tui_gateway/test_profiles_list_worker_session.py` (new, real SessionDB) | 4/4 pass | | `pytest tests/tui_gateway/test_profiles_list_preferred_session.py` | 8/8 pass | | `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` (hermes-bots) | 317/317 pass | | Sabotage run (worker check removed) | new tests fail as intended | ## Infographic ![The working bot is seen](https://files.catbox.moe/r97auo.png)

signal.title: feat(sdk): add host.preview(url) for plugin-driven preview pane opens
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Add a one-line `host.preview(url)` entry to the desktop plugin SDK so a plugin can surface a URL in the right-rail preview pane — the same UX chat uses for tool-result / file-browser / artifact previews. ## Why? The runtime loader (`contrib/runtime-loader.ts`) restricts disk-loaded plugins to `@hermes/plugin-sdk` and `react`; plugins can't import `@/store/preview` directly. Until now there was no first-class SDK door into the preview store, so plugins had no way to hand the user a server UI, dev tool, or web page without leaving the app (e.g. `window.open` to a system browser, or `target=_blank`). Concrete motivator: the DSH settings plugin (`<hermes home>/desktop-plugins/dsh-settings/`) wants a "Open DSH Web UI" button that pops the DSH chat workspace into the right-rail preview pane — same host, same UX as a tool-result preview. ## How `apps/desktop/src/sdk/index.ts` — add `host.preview(url)`: ```ts import { openPreview } from '@/store/preview' … preview: (url: string) => { if (typeof url !== 'string' || !url.trim()) return openPreview({ kind: 'url', label: url, source: 'plugin', url }, 'manual') } ``` `source: 'plugin'` is a free-form discriminator (the type is `string`) — it's recorded so future telemetry / "close all plugin tabs" affordances can find plugin-opened tabs without conflating them with chat / file-browser / artifact previews. `PreviewRecordSource` (`'manual'` here) is the second arg to `openPreview` and only affects HTML file rendering — for URL targets the rendering path is identical to any other `kind: 'url'` target. The `sdkImportMap` in `src/sdk/runtime.ts` re-exports every named export of `./index` as a shim blob, so the new method is automatically available to runtime-loaded disk plugins with zero loader changes. ## Type of Change - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) ## How to Test 1. Open the desktop app, install a disk plugin that calls `host.preview('https://example.com')` (e.g. a debug plugin). 3. Click the button. 4. Right rail focuses the new preview tab showing example.com — same UX as the chat preview on a tool-result. 5. With a file target (e.g. `/tmp/index.html`) loaded via chat preview, verify the new `host.preview` tab is independent (different `source` discriminator, separate tab id). For the DSH settings plugin (the original motivator): once a desktop release with this PR ships, `dsh-settings`'s "Open DSH Web UI" button can be re-pointed from `<a target="_blank">` to `host.preview('http://127.0.0.1:8080/')`. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] Conventional commit message (`feat(sdk): ...`) - [x] Single-file change, no unrelated commits - [x] Diff is +12 lines (1 import + 11 lines incl. doc-comment)
signal.author: branchingjade

signal.title: refactor: reasoning-effort clamps can no longer drift per vendor — one canonical ladder + declared wire vocabularies
signal.text: ## Summary The reasoning-effort bug class can no longer regenerate: one canonical ladder, one clamp policy, and declarative per-route vocabularies replace the 9 hand-rolled per-vendor maps that produced #89503, #70058, #74295 and #87279 one leak at a time. Follow-up to #90330, which fixed the sites; this PR fixes the architecture. Every transport and provider profile now declares *what its wire accepts* (data) and delegates *how to translate* (policy) to a single module. ## Changes - **New `agent/reasoning_effort.py`** — single source of truth: - `EFFORT_LADDER` — canonical low→high ordering (test-pinned superset of `VALID_REASONING_EFFORTS`) - `clamp_effort(effort, supported, overrides)` — one policy: supported passes verbatim; otherwise nearest **weaker** supported level (never escalate cost, never invert the ladder); floor when nothing weaker; `none` is never a degradation target; vendor-documented rounding overrides win; bespoke names pass through - Declared vocabularies as data: OpenAI-compat wire, Codex Responses, xAI (4.6/legacy), Actual relays, Kimi K3/K2, TokenHub, GLM-5.2, DeepSeek V4, Ollama Cloud, Meta, Solar - **Converted call sites** (behavior-preserving unless noted): chat-completions chokepoint + Kimi + TokenHub paths, codex transport, auxiliary client, and the kimi-coding / zai / opencode-zen / deepseek / ollama-cloud / meta-ai / upstage / custom plugins - `hermes_cli.models.clamp_reasoning_effort_to_supported` (openrouter/copilot catalog path) → thin wrapper over the canonical policy - **Behavior fixes the shared policy surfaces:** `minimal` on ollama-cloud/opencode-go now degrades to `low` instead of being silently dropped — dropping left the server default active, i.e. MORE thinking than the user asked for (same inversion class) ## Validation | Contract | Enforced by | |---|---| | Every configurable level clamps into every declared wire set | `test_no_declared_wire_set_contains_ultra` + monotonicity sweep | | Stronger ask never resolves weaker than a weaker ask | `test_monotonic_over_full_ladder` (all declared sets) | | `none` never becomes a degradation target | `test_none_is_never_a_degradation_target` | | No regressions | 620 targeted tests green (transports, all provider profiles, models, lmstudio) | Adding a future model/route = declare its supported set (one tuple, optionally one overrides dict). No new clamp logic, ever. ## Infographic ![one ladder to rule the wires](https://files.catbox.moe/aw7hhf.png)

signal.title: feat(computer_use): pluggable backend providers — one seam for container, sandbox, and remote-desktop runtimes (supersedes #61311)
signal.text: Supersedes [#61311](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/61311) (jarrelscy, credited via `Co-authored-by`). Unblocks [#61507](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/61507) and [#69086](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/69086) as providers rather than as core edits. `computer_use` picked its backend class from a hardcoded two-name branch on `HERMES_COMPUTER_USE_BACKEND`, so the only runtime it could ever drive was cua-driver on the gateway host. Four open PRs are each trying to change that for their own runtime — a Desktop bridge back to the client, a Modal sandbox, a webtop container pool — and each one does it by editing the dispatcher. This is the seam they should all register against instead. ## What lands The host backend becomes a registered provider like any other, so there is exactly one path to a backend: a plugin provider is exercised by the same code the default is, not by a branch nobody runs. - `agent/computer_use_provider.py` — the ABC. Same shape as `BrowserProvider` / `WebSearchProvider`. - `agent/computer_use_registry.py` — registration, unload restore, and `resolve_provider`. - `tools/computer_use/host_provider.py` — `local` (today's cua-driver-on-this-host) and `noop`. - `ctx.register_computer_use_provider()` for plugins. - `computer_use.provider` in `config.yaml`, replacing the env var. ## Two departures from the usual provider ABC **Providers are factories, not caches.** [#61311](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/61311) had providers own a per-`task_id` backend cache, which was right when it was written — `main` has since grown a per-*session* cache with its own call lock, permission mode, and `release_computer_use_session()`. A provider cache on top of that shadows all of it and reintroduces the cross-session bleed the session cache exists to prevent. So a provider only answers "build me one" and the existing lifecycle owns the rest. That is also why the ABC has no `close_backend`: there is no second lifecycle to keep in sync. **An unregistered name raises instead of falling back.** Every other registry can quietly pick a default. Here the default drives the user's own desktop, so silently choosing it for someone who configured a container is the one outcome worth crashing over. The error names the missing provider and the fix, and reaches the user as the tool's output. ## Sweeper findings from [#61311](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/61311) All three are closed: - *Unavailable provider dispatch* — the original raised and caught that in the same `try`, then called `get_backend()` anyway. Availability is now checked before the build, with a dispatch-level test. - *Lifecycle unwired* — `emergency_cleanup()` runs from the atexit hook after every backend is stopped, since leases outlive the backends that drove them. Per session there was nothing to wire: `release_computer_use_session()` already stops the backend. - *`computer_use.cua_driver.*` documented but never read* — dropped. The only key documented here is the one the runtime reads. ## Deliberately not included [#61311](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/61311)'s second commit also hid the tool on headless Linux (`DISPLAY` unset). Defensible, but it removes the tool from people who have it today and is orthogonal to the seam — worth its own PR against its own reports. Resolution is cached per profile home, not per process: under `gateway.multiplex_profiles` one process serves several profiles and reads `computer_use.provider` from each one's own `config.yaml`. The original's single-slot cache would have handed one profile's provider to all of them. ## Test plan - [x] `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/computer_use/test_provider_routing.py` — 29 new tests - [x] `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/computer_use/ tests/tools/test_computer_use*.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins.py` — green except `test_linux_default_capture_skips_gnome_shell_helper`, which fails identically on unmodified `origin/main` (a Linux-behavior test running unmarked on macOS) - [x] `ruff check`, `git diff --check` clean - [x] `HERMES_COMPUTER_USE_BACKEND=noop` still works unchanged — existing tests set it and were not touched

signal.title: codex_app_server runtime reintroduces #15561: a failed turn returns without `failed: true`, so /v1/runs emits run.completed with empty output and zero usage
signal.text: **Version:** hermes-agent 0.20.3 ## Summary #15561 fixed `run.completed`-on-failure for results produced by `run_agent` / `conversation_loop`, by having `_handle_runs` branch on `result["failed"]`. The `codex_app_server` runtime reintroduces the same false-green through a different producer: it reports a failed turn via `completed: False` + `error`, and never sets `failed: True`. The result is a run that terminates as: ```json {"event": "run.completed", "run_id": "run_…", "output": "", "usage": {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0}} ``` with `GET /v1/runs/{id}` reporting `status: "completed"`, `last_event: "run.completed"`, and no `error` — for a turn that failed and produced nothing. ## Impact Any orchestrator that drives Hermes through the API server records a successful run that did no work. For scheduled or unattended agents this is the worst available failure mode: the cadence keeps reporting green, the provider error never surfaces, and no downstream check fires. It is also silent in exactly the situation you most want a signal — the moment a healthy deployment first hits a dead or exhausted provider credential. `run.failed` works correctly for the same underlying fault when the turn is handled by `conversation_loop`, so the symptom is intermittent and looks like flakiness rather than a contract gap. ## Root cause **Producer** — `agent/codex_runtime.py`, terminal return (0.20.3: L917-940, `final_response` at L925): ```python return { "final_response": turn.final_text, # "" when the turn errored "messages": messages, "api_calls": api_calls, "completed": not turn.interrupted and turn.error is None, # False "partial": turn.interrupted or turn.error is not None, # True "interrupted": _user_interrupted, "error": turn.error, # the error IS carried ... # but no "failed": True } ``` Reached after the `should_retire` handler (L806-820) has already logged the turn error: ``` WARNING agent.codex_runtime: codex app-server session retired (turn error: <provider error>) ``` **Consumer** — `gateway/platforms/api_server.py`, `_handle_runs` (0.20.3: L6953, L6968): ```python elif isinstance(result, dict) and result.get("failed"): -> run.failed else: final_response = result.get("final_response", "") if isinstance(result, dict) else "" -> run.completed, output=final_response, usage=usage ``` `completed: False` and a non-null `error` are both ignored, so the result falls to the `run.completed` branch and `final_response` defaults to `""`. `agent/conversation_loop.py` does set `failed: True` on its failure paths, which is why #15561's fix holds there and not here. ## Reproduction ### Unit-level (no credentials required) Feed a `codex_app_server`-shaped result through the terminal branch of `_handle_runs`: ```python result = { "final_response": "", "messages": [], "api_calls": 1, "completed": False, "partial": True, "interrupted": False, "error": "turn ended status=failed: <provider error>", } usage = {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0} # expected: run.failed, error preserved # actual: run.completed, output="", usage.total_tokens=0 ``` ### Observed end to end On an API-server lane configured with `model.openai_runtime: codex_app_server`, against a provider whose credential had been revoked server-side: - run terminated `completed` / `output: ""` / `total_tokens: 0`, at the same second the journal logged `agent.codex_runtime: codex app-server session retired (turn error: Codex authentication failed …)`; - a subsequent run against the identical fault was handled by `conversation_loop` (`ERROR agent.conversation_loop: Non-retryable client error: 401`) and correctly emitted `run.failed`. Observed twice. It is not currently forceable on demand from our side: once the credential is fully revoked, the auth gate short-circuits ahead of the codex transport and every run takes the correctly-failing `conversation_loop` path. Reaching the faulty path needs a codex turn that *starts* and then errors — e.g. a mid-turn child failure or a tripped post-tool watchdog, both of which set `should_retire`. We are filing on the code analysis rather than holding for a live recipe; the producer/consumer behaviour above was verified against the pinned 0.20.3 sources. ## Suggested fix — both sides **1. Producer.** Have the `codex_app_server` terminal return set `"failed": True` whenever `turn.error` is not None, matching the contract `conversation_loop` already follows. **2. Consumer defence.** In `_handle_runs`, do not emit `run.completed` when `error` is non-null or `completed` is `False`, even if a runtime omitted `failed`: ```python elif isinstance(result, dict) and ( result.get("failed") or result.get("error") or result.get("completed") is False ): -> run.failed ``` Either change alone closes the observed case. We'd argue for both: #15561 chose the narrow producer-flag check, and this issue is that decision regressing the moment a second runtime reached the same consumer. A terminal status that downstream automation trusts should not depend on every current and future runtime remembering to set one optional key. Related: #15561 (closed, same class, `conversation_loop` producer), #71633 (`codex_app_server` bypasses `fallback_providers` on billing/quota failures — adjacent, same runtime, distinct defect).

signal.title: False-positive "TERMINAL_CWD found in .env" deprecation warning on every startup
signal.text: Every TUI startup prints this even though `.env` never sets `TERMINAL_CWD`: ``` ⚠ Deprecated .env settings detected: ⚠ TERMINAL_CWD=/Users/you found in .env — this is deprecated. ``` **Root cause** `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` in `hermes_cli/config.py` decides ".env sets TERMINAL_CWD" from the process environment alone. But Hermes exports that variable into `os.environ` itself at runtime: `gateway/run.py:2504`, `cli.py:8473` (session restore), `cron/scheduler.py:5087` (per job), `tui_gateway/server.py:12559`, plus the worktree paths in `cli.py:20298` and `hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py:1287`. So any install where `config.yaml` keeps the default `terminal.cwd: .` (which doesn't count as "explicit" in the checker) warns on every startup, with nothing to migrate. The config-to-env bridge is not the setter either; it explicitly skips `cwd: .`. **Repro** 1. Clean `~/.hermes/.env` with no `TERMINAL_CWD` line 2. `config.yaml` with default `terminal.cwd: .` (or no terminal section) 3. Start the TUI after any code path above has run (gateway, session restore, cron) 4. Warning prints, and the suggested migration is a no-op **Fix** Gate the warning on what `.env` actually contains: read `HERMES_HOME/.env` and warn only when an uncommented `TERMINAL_CWD=` (or `export TERMINAL_CWD=`) line exists. Same for `MESSAGING_CWD`. Patch with a regression test is ready; PR to follow.

signal.title: [Bug]: False-positive "Deprecated .env settings" TERMINAL_CWD warning on plain `hermes chat -q` (incidental gateway.run import from relay_runtime)
signal.text: ### Bug Description Hermes v0.20.4 (Linux, local terminal backend, `terminal.cwd: .` in config.yaml) prints a false-positive deprecation warning on every chat startup: ``` ⚠ Deprecated .env settings detected: ⚠ TERMINAL_CWD=/root found in .env — this is deprecated. Move to config.yaml instead: terminal: cwd: /your/project/path Then remove the old entries from ~/.hermes/.env ``` even though `TERMINAL_CWD` is **not set anywhere in `~/.hermes/.env`** (line 214 is commented out: `# TERMINAL_CWD=.`). ### Steps to Reproduce 1. config.yaml: `terminal: { backend: local, cwd: . }` 2. `~/.hermes/.env` has no uncommented `TERMINAL_CWD` 3. Run from any directory: `hermes chat -q "x"` 4. Warning appears on stderr before the reply Reproducible even with a pristine environment (`env -i` with only PATH/HOME/SHELL/LANG/TERM), i.e. not caused by any stale shell export. ### Root Cause (traced) The emitting call site is **`gateway/run.py:2441-2444`** — module-level code that runs whenever `gateway.run` is imported. On the plain CLI path (no gateway involved), this import happens incidentally: ``` hermes chat -q x → run_agent.run_conversation → agent.relay_runtime.begin_turn → relay_runtime._segments_config() (relay_runtime.py:174) → from gateway.run import _load_gateway_config # late import → gateway/run.py module-level warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars() (line 2444) ``` Underlying problem: `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` inspects `os.environ` (not the .env file), and `cli.py`'s own config bridge force-exports `terminal.cwd` into `TERMINAL_CWD` at startup (cli.py ~line 700). So the warning reports a value that Hermes itself put there — it cannot distinguish a bridged value from a genuine .env entry. The check also runs before `load_hermes_dotenv()` re-applies the config bridge. The "remove from ~/.hermes/.env" hint is misleading because the value never came from .env. ### Expected Behavior No deprecation warning when `TERMINAL_CWD` is not set in `.env`, regardless of what os.environ contains (bridged, restored-session, or worktree values are all legitimate runtime state). ### Workaround (confirmed on 0.20.4) `hermes config set terminal.cwd /root` — an explicit path short-circuits the warning. Verified clean across: bridged value equal to cwd, exported foreign value, and no-value cases. ### Related - #88829 (config-bridge self-report, CLI startup) — this issue adds the second trigger path (relay_runtime → gateway.run) that fires per-turn on plain chat, not just startup - #89016 (terminal.cwd='.' local backend) — PR #89124 has a fix for the startup path - #85695 (gateway start) - Fix PRs under review: #87034, #88533, #88552, #89124 ### Suggested Fix 1. Read deprecated-cwd vars from the .env file itself (as #87034/#88533/#89124 propose) instead of os.environ, and 2. Guard the module-level call in `gateway/run.py` so the warning only runs when the gateway is the actual entry point (not on incidental late imports from relay_runtime / oneshot / CLI tool paths).

signal.title: False-positive 'Deprecated .env settings' warning when terminal.cwd is '.' (local backend)
signal.text: ## Summary False-positive **"Deprecated .env settings detected"** warning on every startup when `terminal.cwd` is set to `.` (follow-the-launch-dir) with the local terminal backend — even though `.env` no longer contains `TERMINAL_CWD`. ## Reproduction 1. `config.yaml`: ```yaml terminal: cwd: . ``` 2. `.env` has no uncommented `TERMINAL_CWD` (in my case it is commented out: `# TERMINAL_CWD=.`). 3. Launch `hermes` (CLI or TUI) from any directory. Observed warning (stderr): ``` ⚠ Deprecated .env settings detected: ⚠ TERMINAL_CWD=<absolute launch dir> found in .env — this is deprecated. Move to config.yaml instead: terminal: cwd: /your/project/path Then remove the old entries from <hermes home>/.env ``` ## Expected No warning. `TERMINAL_CWD` is bridged from `terminal.cwd` by the CLI itself, not a leftover `.env` entry. `.` is the documented way to keep the working directory as the launch directory. ## Actual Warning printed at every startup. Functionality is unaffected (cwd resolution works), but the warning is misleading — there is nothing to migrate. ## Root cause `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars` in `hermes_cli/config.py:2190` detects the deprecation by reading the **environment variable** `os.environ.get("TERMINAL_CWD")` (config.py:2196-2197), not by inspecting the `.env` file. Meanwhile the CLI bridge in `cli.py:649-651` **always overwrites** `terminal.cwd` with `os.getcwd()` for the local backend: ```python if effective_backend == "local": terminal_config["cwd"] = os.getcwd() ``` and force-exports it (`cli.py:700-704`): `os.environ["TERMINAL_CWD"] = str(terminal_config[config_key])`. Additionally, `config_has_explicit_cwd` excludes placeholder values `{".", "auto", "cwd", ""}` (config.py:2208), so `cwd: .` is treated as "no explicit path" and the warning fires even though the env var was produced by the config bridge, not `.env`. The check cannot distinguish a config-bridged value from a genuine `.env` leftover. ## Suggested fix - Read the `.env` file directly (parse for an uncommented `TERMINAL_CWD=` line) instead of sampling the environment, and/or - Skip the warning when the current `TERMINAL_CWD` equals the config-bridged value (e.g. the launch dir substituted for `.` by the local backend), and/or - Treat `.` (and the shared placeholder set `{".", "auto", "cwd"}` already defined at `cli.py:646`) as an explicit user intent in `config_has_explicit_cwd`. ## Environment - OS: Windows 11, git-bash shell - Hermes Agent v0.20.3 (2026.8.16.2), install dir `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent` - Python 3.11.15 - Local terminal backend (`terminal.env_type` unset / local)

signal.text: ### Bug Description ## Bug Description The CLI startup prints a false-positive deprecation warning: ``` ⚠ Deprecated .env settings detected: ⚠ TERMINAL_CWD=/mnt/c/Users/andyf found in .env — this is deprecated. ``` ...even though `TERMINAL_CWD` is **not** set anywhere in `~/.hermes/.env` (verified: the file has no such entry, Windows registry env vars are clean, and a fresh WSL session has no such variable). ## Root Cause Two pieces of code contradict each other: 1. `cli.py` (~line 694-702) **force-exports** `terminal.cwd` from `config.yaml` into `os.environ["TERMINAL_CWD"]` (comment says: "CLI: always export (overrides stale .env or inherited values)"). With a default `cwd: .`, the exported value is the resolved absolute startup path. 2. `hermes_cli/config.py` `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` (line 2182) reads `os.environ.get("TERMINAL_CWD")` and, when `config.terminal.cwd` is not an "explicit path" (i.e. one of `.`, `auto`, `cwd`, `""`), assumes the variable must have come from `.env` and warns. So Hermes exports the variable itself and then warns about itself. Any stock config with `cwd: .` triggers the warning on every startup. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. `config.yaml` has `terminal.cwd: .` (the default) 2. `.env` contains no `TERMINAL_CWD` line 3. Start the CLI (`hermes`) 4. Observe the deprecation warning despite nothing being set in `.env` ## Expected Behavior No warning when the variable was not set by the user in `.env` — in particular, no warning when `os.environ["TERMINAL_CWD"]` exactly matches the value the config bridge itself exported. ## Suggested Fix - In `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()`, skip the warning when `os.environ["TERMINAL_CWD"]` equals the resolved value of `terminal.cwd` (e.g. `str(Path(cwd).resolve())`), or pass an explicit flag from the bridge context; **or** - Have the bridge skip exporting `TERMINAL_CWD` when the config value is non-explicit (`.`, `auto`, `cwd`, `""`). ## Environment - Hermes Agent v0.20.2 (2026.8.16) - WSL2 (Ubuntu), local terminal backend - CLI (not gateway) ### Steps to Reproduce 1. config.yaml has terminal.cwd: . (the default) 2. .env contains no TERMINAL_CWD line 3. Start the CLI (hermes) 4. Observe the deprecation warning despite nothing being set in .env ### Expected Behavior No warning when TERMINAL_CWD was not set by the user in .env — especially when the env var value matches the one the config bridge exported itself. ### Actual Behavior CLI prints "⚠ Deprecated .env settings detected: TERMINAL_CWD=/mnt/c/Users/andyf found in .env" on every startup, even though .env has no such entry (verified). Root cause: cli.py force-exports terminal.cwd into os.environ["TERMINAL_CWD"], then warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars() (hermes_cli/config.py:2182) sees it and misattributes it to .env. ### Affected Component CLI (interactive chat) ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A (CLI only) ### Debug Report ```shell N/A — prefer not to upload personal data ``` ### Operating System Ubuntu 22.04 ### Python Version _No response_ ### Hermes Version _No response_ ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) _No response_ ### Proposed Fix (optional) _No response_ ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR
