signal.title: False positive: "TERMINAL_CWD deprecated" warning on every gateway start (env var, not .env)
signal.text: ## Summary Hermes shows a deprecation warning on every start even though the user **never set** `TERMINAL_CWD` in `~/.hermes/.env` (the only occurrence is a commented-out `# TERMINAL_CWD=.`): ``` ⚠ Deprecated .env settings detected: ⚠ TERMINAL_CWD=/path/to/project found in .env — this is deprecated. Move to config.yaml instead: terminal: cwd: /your/project/path Then remove the old entries from ~/.hermes/.env ``` ## Root cause (traced in source) 1. `cli.py:7706` (`_restore_session_cwd`) sets `os.environ["TERMINAL_CWD"]` when a session with a recorded cwd is resumed (`/resume`, `--resume`, continuing an old session). The env var then **outlives the session** and sticks to the shell/process env. 2. `gateway/run.py:2395` calls `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()`, which reads `os.environ.get("TERMINAL_CWD")` (config.py:2151) — i.e. **process env**, not the .env **file**. 3. `doctor.py:436-437` explicitly documents the intended behavior: deprecated env vars should be *"checked in the .env file, not process env, so config→env bridges like terminal.cwd → TERMINAL_CWD do not false-positive."* So `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` contradicts doctor.py: it checks process env, which the config bridge / session-restore populates legitimately, and reports a user-facing deprecation warning that is a false positive. ## Repro - Any session whose process env already contains `TERMINAL_CWD` (e.g. after resuming a session created in a project dir). - `env -u TERMINAL_CWD hermes chat -q ok` suppresses the warning; with `TERMINAL_CWD` set it appears. Verified: with env set → 1 warning, without → 0. ## Expected `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` should read the **.env file** (like `doctor.py` does) instead of `os.environ`, so a launch-artifact / config-bridge value never triggers a user-facing "you have a deprecated setting" warning. At minimum, skip the warning when `terminal.cwd` in config.yaml is non-explicit (".") and the env value matches the session-restore path. ## Environment - Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13) - OS: Linux Mint - Source: cli

signal.title: fix(config): stop runtime CWD values from triggering dotenv warnings
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Stops Hermes from reporting `TERMINAL_CWD` or `MESSAGING_CWD` as deprecated `.env` settings when those values exist only in the process environment. Gateway starts and resumed sessions no longer show a false migration warning, while real deprecated entries on disk continue to produce the warning. ### Symptom Starting the gateway with a runtime-populated `TERMINAL_CWD` prints a warning claiming that the value was found in `.env`, even when `.env` contains no active entry. ### Impact Affected users see an incorrect deprecation warning on every gateway start and are instructed to remove a setting that is not present in their `.env` file. This obscures legitimate migration warnings and makes normal config bridges or session restoration appear misconfigured. ### Bug Cause **Trigger:** `hermes_cli/config.py` / `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` reading `os.environ` **Causal chain:** 1. Runtime config bridging or session restoration places `TERMINAL_CWD` in the process environment. 2. `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` reads the merged process environment instead of the `.env` file it claims to diagnose. 3. Hermes reports the runtime-only value as a deprecated `.env` entry. **Why it is wrong:** Process environment provenance cannot distinguish a user-authored `.env` entry from legitimate runtime state, so the warning attributes values to the wrong source. **Working sibling / contrast:** The doctor diagnostic already checks parsed `.env` contents rather than process environment values, which avoids this false positive. **Ruled out:** A commented `# TERMINAL_CWD=.` line is not parsed as an active setting; regression coverage confirms commented and empty values remain silent. ### Fix Read deprecated CWD settings through the existing `.env` parser, trim empty values, and warn for every real deprecated disk entry regardless of the current `terminal.cwd` config. Regression tests cover process-only values, both deprecated disk entries, explicit config combined with a legacy disk entry, and commented or empty values. ## Related Issue Fixes #85695 ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `hermes_cli/config.py` - inspect parsed `.env` values instead of `os.environ` when emitting CWD migration warnings. - `tests/hermes_cli/test_deprecated_cwd_warning.py` - add provenance and legacy-entry behavior coverage. ## How to Test 1. Put only a commented `# TERMINAL_CWD=.` entry in `.env`, set `TERMINAL_CWD` in the process environment, and confirm no deprecation warning is emitted. 2. Add an active `TERMINAL_CWD=/legacy/path` entry to `.env` and confirm the migration warning is emitted, including when `terminal.cwd` is explicitly configured. 3. Automated (already run locally, 56 passed): ```bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_deprecated_cwd_warning.py tests/hermes_cli/test_doctor.py ``` ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] Relevant documentation update: N/A - no user-facing configuration contract changed - [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` update: N/A - no config keys changed - [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` update: N/A - no architecture or workflow changed - [x] Cross-platform impact considered - `.env` parsing is shared across supported platforms - [x] Tool descriptions/schemas update: N/A - no model tool behavior changed ## Screenshots / Logs Targeted test suite: 56 passed.

signal.title: fix(cli): read .env (not os.environ) for deprecated cwd warning
signal.text: ## Problem `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` reads `TERMINAL_CWD` / `MESSAGING_CWD` from `os.environ`. But the CLI itself exports `TERMINAL_CWD` into the process environment at runtime when restoring a session's working directory (and a gateway restarted from such a session inherits it). This produces a **false-positive** deprecation warning on every startup even when the user has already migrated the setting to `terminal.cwd` in `config.yaml` and there is **no** `TERMINAL_CWD` in `.env` at all. ## Fix Read the on-disk `.env` via `load_env()` instead of `os.environ`, so only a genuine `.env` entry triggers the warning. Runtime-bridged values no longer false-positive. ## Test Added a regression test (`test_process_env_alone_does_not_warn`) asserting that a `TERMINAL_CWD` present only in the process environment (not in `.env`) does not warn. Existing tests updated to stub `load_env` instead of `monkeypatch.setenv`. ``` tests/hermes_cli/test_deprecated_cwd_warning.py ... 3 passed ```

signal.title: fix(config): prevent false-positive deprecated cwd warning for bridged local cwd (#89016)
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #89016. When `terminal.cwd` is set to `.` (the default/documented follow-the-launch-dir setting for the local backend), the CLI bridge exports `os.environ['TERMINAL_CWD'] = os.getcwd()`. `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` was checking only the presence of `TERMINAL_CWD` in the process environment and whether `terminal.cwd` was an explicit non-placeholder path, leading to a misleading 'Deprecated .env settings detected' warning on every startup even when `.env` contained no such key. ## Changes - In `hermes_cli/config.py` (`warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars`): - Read from `load_env()` to check if `TERMINAL_CWD` is truly present in `.env`. - Skip the deprecation warning when `TERMINAL_CWD` was bridged by the local backend and is not present in `.env`. - In `tests/hermes_cli/test_deprecated_cwd_warning.py`: - Added test `test_local_backend_dot_cwd_does_not_warn_when_bridged`. - Added test `test_dot_env_terminal_cwd_warns`. ## Verification - `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_deprecated_cwd_warning.py tests/hermes_cli/test_config.py tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py` passed (83/83 passed). - GPG signed on Mac and `git diff --check` clean.

signal.title: fix: warn about deprecated cwd env vars only when they are in .env
signal.text: ## Problem Every CLI/gateway startup on my machine printed: ``` ⚠ Deprecated .env settings detected: ⚠ TERMINAL_CWD=/Users/jashlee found in .env — this is deprecated. Then remove the old entries from ~/.hermes/.env ``` My `~/.hermes/.env` has no `TERMINAL_CWD` line. The warning tells the user to delete something that isn't there, and there is no way to make it stop. ## Root cause `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` (`hermes_cli/config.py`) reads `os.environ["TERMINAL_CWD"]` and reports it as "found in .env". It never opens `.env`. But `TERMINAL_CWD` is set at runtime by several unrelated paths: - the `terminal.cwd` → `TERMINAL_CWD` config bridge (`TERMINAL_CONFIG_ENV_MAP`) - session-cwd restore on resume (`cli.py:8378`) - worktree switch (`cli_commands_mixin.py:1287`, `main.py:2738`) - gateway placeholder resolution (`gateway/run.py:2492`) - kanban workspace pinning (`kanban_db.py:10787`) - cron per-job workdir (`cron/scheduler.py:4965`) Any of those false-positives. `hermes doctor` already got this right — `doctor.py:1526` reads the on-disk `.env` with the comment *"Prefer the on-disk .env so bridged process env (e.g. TERMINAL_CWD from terminal.cwd) does not false-positive."* The startup warning just never got the same treatment. ## Fix Read `load_env()` (the on-disk `.env` parser already used by doctor) instead of `os.environ`, and return early when neither key is present. The `config_has_explicit_cwd` suppression below it is left alone. ## Verification - `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_deprecated_cwd_warning.py` → 3 passed. - Teeth check: reverted `config.py` to the pre-fix version with the new tests in place → 3/3 fail, including the new `test_runtime_terminal_cwd_does_not_warn`. The test fails on known-bad. - `ruff check` clean on both changed files. The existing two tests set the vars via `monkeypatch.setenv`, which no longer describes the contract; they now write a real `.env` under a temp `HERMES_HOME`. Added `test_runtime_terminal_cwd_does_not_warn` as the regression case for the reported symptom. ## Known / out of scope - `MESSAGING_CWD` is deliberately still warned about from the file — it has no config-bridge writer, so it can only come from `.env`; reading the file is correct for it too and keeps one code path. - No UI/perf surface changed, so no screenshots or benchmarks apply.

signal.title: fix: read deprecated cwd vars from .env file, not os.environ
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes a false-positive in the startup deprecation warning: `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` claimed `TERMINAL_CWD` / `MESSAGING_CWD` were "found in .env" by reading **`os.environ`**, not the `.env` file. Hermes bridges `terminal.cwd` into `TERMINAL_CWD` in the process environment at startup (gateway config bridge), so an `os.environ` read falsely triggers the warning even when: - the user never wrote the deprecated var to `.env`, and - the `.env` line is commented out (e.g. `# TERMINAL_CWD=.`). ## Root cause `hermes_cli/config.py` → `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()`: ```python terminal_cwd_env = os.environ.get("TERMINAL_CWD") # reads env, not .env ... if terminal_cwd_env and not config_has_explicit_cwd: # "TERMINAL_CWD=... found in .env — this is deprecated." ``` The comment in the original code even says "likely from .env" — it never checks the file. Since Hermes itself injects `TERMINAL_CWD` into the environment (resolving the `.` placeholder to `Path.home()` and bridging terminal config to `TERMINAL_*` vars), every startup with `terminal.cwd: .` in config.yaml and a Hermes-injected env emits a spurious migration warning. ## Fix Read the deprecated vars from the **`.env` file** via the existing `load_env()` helper (which skips comment/blank lines), not from `os.environ`: - `.env` entry present → warning still fires (migration is genuinely needed). - Only ambient env var / Hermes bridge → no warning. ## Tests Added/updated in `tests/hermes_cli/test_deprecated_cwd_warning.py`: - `test_messaging_cwd_triggers_warning` — env vars set but only `.env` content matters; `TERMINAL_CWD` absent from `.env` must not warn. - `test_both_deprecated_vars_warn` — both vars in `.env` warn. - `test_terminal_cwd_ignored_when_config_has_explicit_cwd` — explicit `terminal.cwd` in config.yaml suppresses the warning. - `test_env_var_without_dotenv_entry_does_not_warn` — **regression**: `TERMINAL_CWD` in `os.environ` (Hermes bridge) but absent from `.env` must not warn. Verification: - `tests/hermes_cli/test_deprecated_cwd_warning.py`: 4 passed. - End-to-end with a temp `HERMES_HOME`: env-only var → no warning; `.env` entry → warning emitted with correct hint. - Broader `tests/hermes_cli -k "config or env or dotenv or cwd"`: 917 passed; 32 failures reproduce independently of this change (browser-install / venv-health tests, pass when run in isolation).
signal.author: zhwen

signal.title: fix(agent): stop tool loops across result-hash and arg jitter
signal.text: ## Summary The no-progress detector keyed on `(signature, result_hash)`, so any repeat whose *result* differed reset the streak. Two mechanisms exploited that in live sessions, and a third survived even after signature counting: 1. The context compressor rewrites an older duplicate tool body to `[Duplicate tool output ...]`, which changes the hash. 2. Tools that vary their payload for a repeat call by design (`skill_view` returns `status: "unchanged"`) never look like a repeated result. 3. Even after counting identical signatures, a loop could mint a *fresh* signature every iteration by jittering one irrelevant field (`todo` alternating `merge: true`/`false` while re-asserting a byte-identical list). Repeating an identical call is the loop; the shape of the response is not what makes it one. This PR stacks three commits: - `bcb9e0374` — count identical **signatures**, not identical result hashes. Applies to every tool, including mutating bookkeeping tools like `todo`. Membership in `MUTATING_TOOL_NAMES` is not evidence of progress. - `ba0330f1e` — carry no-progress streaks across turn boundaries. `reset_for_turn()` no longer wipes `_no_progress`; streaks clear only when the world actually moves, gated on `file_mutation_result_landed()`. - `c1d9de8f5` — close the remaining two holes: normalize declarative `todo` payloads before hashing (item order + `merge` do not change the asserted end state), and collapse the compressor duplicate stub to a stable sentinel in `_result_hash()`. A landed file mutation still resets its own signature count, so write → re-run → write cycles and post-edit re-verification stay allowed. ## Test plan - [x] `tests/agent/test_tool_guardrails.py` + related runtime/sidecar tests: **82 passed** on `c1d9de8f5` with the repo venv (`~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python`, pytest 9.1.1, Python 3.11.15). - [x] Mutation-kill of `c1d9de8f5`: disabling arg normalization fails 2 tests; disabling the duplicate sentinel fails 1; byte-exact restore returns 12/12 green. - [ ] CI on this PR. Do not merge from review. Draft until the author decides.

signal.title: feat(agent): repeat-tool-reminder advisory (loop hygiene)
signal.text: ## Summary Adds advisory loop hygiene: consecutive identical tool calls (same tool name + canonically identical arguments) get a soft reminder appended to the tail of the current tool result when the run length hits a threshold — escalating tone at 3, 5, and 8 repeats. Root cause: models can loop on the same tool call with identical arguments, burning tokens on every repeated step (and each loop step is a new request that can invalidate the cached prefix). A non-blocking reminder lets the model self-correct without vetoing anything. ## Changes - `agent/repeat_tool_reminder.py` (new): `canonicalize_arguments` (reuses `canonical_tool_args` — deep key-sorted JSON), `wildcard_to_regex` (anchored, `*` → `.*`), per-agent chain with lock, thresholds `[3, 5, 8]` gentle→detailed escalation, `gentle_reminder`/`detailed_reminder` with stable `[reminder]` prefix and capped args preview, `reset`; advisory contract — any exception → `None`, never breaks the loop - `agent/tool_dispatch_helpers.py`: `make_tool_result_message(..., append_tail=None)` — appended at the END, AFTER the untrusted-content wrapping (the reminder never becomes untrusted data; cached prefix stays byte-identical) - `agent/tool_executor.py`: `maybe_remind` in both mount points (sequential + concurrent, using `name`/`args` from parsed calls, correct across success/timeout/cancel/block outcomes) - `agent/conversation_loop.py`: reset on real user message (new turn and mid-turn redirect) - `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py` + `cli-config.yaml.example`: `repeat_tool_reminder` section — `enabled` (default true), `thresholds`, `include`/`exclude` wildcards, `arguments_preview_chars` - `tests/agent/test_repeat_tool_reminder.py` (new, 25 tests) + `tests/agent/test_tool_dispatch_helpers.py` updated ## Validation | Teste | Resultado | |-------|-----------| | `pytest tests/agent/test_repeat_tool_reminder.py tests/agent/test_tool_dispatch_helpers.py` | 54 passed | | Non-blocking contract | reminder appends only; execution never vetoed (tested) |

signal.title: fix(desktop): deleting an archived session no longer leaves a ghost row that spins forever
signal.text: ## Summary Deleting a session from the sidebar's Archived filter no longer leaves a ghost row whose click spins forever. Root cause: archived rows render from `$archivedSessions` — a separate capped store (archived rows are excluded from `$sessions` by design) — but `removeSession` only pruned `$sessions`. The surviving ghost row then resumed into a hard-deleted id: resume 404 → `goneSessionVerdict` saw the row still listed (`stillListed=true`) → verdict `retry` → an unrecoverable spinner with the composer unmounted. ## Changes - `use-session-actions/index.ts`: `removeSession` resolves the row from `$sessions` OR `$archivedSessions`, evicts it from both stores optimistically, and restores the archived row on RPC failure (rollback parity with the main list). Resolving from the archived store also means `deleteSession` now receives the row's owning `profile` for archived rows. - `remove-archived-session.test.tsx`: 3 tests — eviction on success, restore on failure, profile forwarding. ## Validation | | Result | |---|---| | New tests | 3/3 pass | | Sabotage run (fix stashed) | 2/3 fail as intended | | Sibling use-session-actions suites | 182/182 pass | | Live desktop: archive → Archived filter → delete | row gone from view + state.db, no spinner | Found during the full-desktop feature audit (Aug 19): deterministic repro was archive session → enable Archived filter → delete → click remaining row. ## Infographic ![Archived delete no more ghost row](https://files.catbox.moe/m4rytk.png)

signal.title: [Proposal]: Unify Desktop Preview and Browser into a human-agent Workspace Viewer
signal.text: ## Summary Hermes Desktop now has several strong but separate content and browser-adjacent experiences: - a preview rail for files and generated artefacts - rendered Markdown, source, diff and editing - image and PDF viewers - inline audio and video players in chat - a persistent in-app Browser webview with address bar, history, console and DevTools - `open_preview` / `read_preview` for the agent - separate `browser_*` / `browser_exec` automation backends The individual pieces are useful, but the product model is fragmented. A non-technical user should not need to understand whether something is a preview, artefact, attachment, webview or separate agent-browser session. A developer should not lose console, source, diff, DevTools or browser-routing control in order to get a simpler default experience. This issue proposes a product direction for feedback before implementation: evolve the existing preview rail into one cohesive, progressively disclosed **Workspace Viewer**, with explicit human/agent control handoff for visible browser work. ## Current behaviour and gap The URL mode in the preview rail is already a real persistent Electron `<webview>`: - address bar, back/forward/reload - console and DevTools - persistent cookies through `persist:hermes-preview` - agent-side open and read access However: 1. The visible Browser is still architecturally separate from semantic agent browser automation. 2. URL browsing is a singleton surface, while files and artefacts use separate preview tabs. 3. Audio and video play inline in chat but are not dedicated preview-tab file types. 4. There is no explicit **Take control / Return to Hermes** ownership contract for login, CAPTCHA, 2FA or other human-only steps. 5. The visible UI exposes the implementation history rather than one mental model for “what I am viewing or working on”. 6. On macOS, a live test found that 1Password Universal Autofill did not work inside the Hermes Browser webview, so login cannot currently rely on ordinary app-level autofill. ## Proposed product direction Present the surface to users as one **Viewer** while retaining advanced capabilities through progressive disclosure. ### Ordinary-user default - A visible **Open Viewer** entry offers **Browse the web**, **Open a file** and **View recent output**. - Websites, Markdown, documents, images, PDFs, media and generated artefacts open in one consistent tabbed surface. - Controls are content-aware rather than universal clutter. - A web tab clearly shows either **Hermes is working** or **Your turn**. - The user can choose **Take control**, complete a login or verification step, then choose **Return to Hermes**. - Infrastructure terms such as CDP, webContents IDs, providers and capability manifests stay out of the default flow. ### Developer and power-user disclosure - rendered/source/diff/edit modes - console and DevTools - viewport presets - inspect element or selected source lines → add to chat - multiple tabs and restored workspaces, once exact tab identity is safe - optional browser-source selection: visible Viewer, isolated local browser, cloud browser or explicitly granted existing profile - exact session/target diagnostics under Advanced The intent is not to remove technical control. It is to hide it until requested. ## Human/agent ownership contract A visible authenticated browser needs one unambiguous owner at a time. Suggested states: - human - agent active - waiting for human - verifying handoff - blocked/disconnected Suggested flow: 1. Hermes works visibly in the bound tab. 2. A human-only step is detected or requested. 3. The tab changes to **Your turn** and agent mutation authority is revoked. 4. The user completes the step without exposing credentials to the model. 5. The user selects **Return to Hermes**. 6. Hermes performs a read-only verification and resumes only if the exact tab generation is still valid. Once a turn is bound to the visible Viewer, failure must not silently route actions to a different local, cloud or headless browser. ## Security constraints - Exact profile, conversation, window, tab, webContents and generation binding. - UI ownership state must be backed by runtime enforcement. - Stale, closed, navigated or replaced tab capabilities fail closed. - Passwords, OTPs and passkeys must never cross model context, tool arguments/results, transcripts, logs or clipboard. - Existing-profile and site access remain explicit opt-ins. - Multiple tabs should come only after exact identity and ownership are proven. - Authentication may require a native user-initiated credential broker if OS/browser autofill cannot work, but that should be scoped separately after the ownership direction is accepted. ## Suggested staged delivery This is intentionally not proposed as one large PR. 1. **UX proposal/prototype:** validate mixed-content tabs and human handoff language. 2. **Cohesive Viewer shell:** discoverable open action, consistent tab chrome and audio/video file tabs, without changing automation authority. 3. **Ownership state machine:** Take control / Return to Hermes with fail-safe lifecycle. 4. **Read-only exact-tab bridge:** URL, title, snapshot, text and screenshot. 5. **Bounded visible mutations:** click, non-secret type, press, scroll and navigation. 6. **Authentication assistance:** separately scoped, user-initiated and secret-safe. 7. **Multiple web tabs and expert routing:** only after identity/ownership are mature. Each stage should be independently reviewable and useful. ## Relationship to existing work - #69951 asked for an in-app browser pane driven by browser tooling. The visible pane now exists; the agent-control half remains unresolved. - #89146 covers the narrow Open Browser discoverability gap and should retain ownership of that slice. - #84000 and PRs #85351 / #88203 explore a Chrome-extension shared-control lane. That is complementary but does not automatically bind the Desktop preview webview. - #89602 documents the macOS platform-passkey limitation in the embedded Browser. - #71375 covers browser-tool tab management rather than the Desktop Viewer product model. This proposal should build on those owners rather than replace or duplicate their work. ## Direction questions for maintainers 1. Is the current preview rail intended to evolve into a first-class mixed-content Viewer, or should the visible Browser remain a lightweight preview surface? 2. Should semantic agent browser automation eventually bind to the visible Desktop webview, or should visible human-assisted browsing remain a Chrome-extension/external-browser concern? 3. Does an explicit human/agent ownership contract fit the desired Desktop architecture? 4. Would the team prefer an interactive UX prototype/RFC before any production PRs? 5. If the direction is welcome, which narrow slice should be pursued first while preserving the existing issue/PR owners? ## Acceptance criteria for this issue This issue is successful if it produces architectural and product-direction feedback. It is not requesting approval for a platform-sized implementation in one PR.

signal.title: fix(desktop): Enter confirms a clicked clarify choice
signal.text: ## Summary In the clarify tool card, **clicking a choice leaves focus on the option button**. The global keydown handler's focus guard treated *any* focused button as hands-off: ```ts if (active && (active.isContentEditable || active.matches('a[href], button, input, ...'))) { return // hands-off } ``` So pressing **Enter** after clicking a choice fell through to the button's native behavior — its `onClick` is `selectChoice`, which just re-selects. The user had to click **Continue** manually. ## Fix Choice rows are the answer itself: when the focused element is `button[data-choice]`, Enter now runs the normal activate/confirm path (which submits a staged/picked answer). The guard still stands down for every other focused control (Skip, Continue, the Other textarea, composer). ## Test Plan - New regression test: `confirms a clicked choice with Enter while the choice button keeps focus` — click → focus stays on the option → Enter → `clarify.respond` called with the picked answer - Existing suite still green (19 tests in clarify-tool.test.tsx, incl. 'does not intercept keyboard events while an action button has focus')

signal.title: [Bug]: Clean TUI shutdown logs an unhandled BrokenPipeError from _log_exit (unguarded stderr write on the peer-closed path)
signal.text: ## Summary On a normal TUI shutdown, the gateway child dies with an unhandled `BrokenPipeError` **inside the handler that reports the clean exit**. The process was already exiting, so nothing is lost — but every ordinary TUI close writes a traceback into `~/.hermes/logs/tui_gateway_crash.log`, which makes routine teardown look like a crash. ``` === gateway exit · 2026-08-19 12:23:47 · reason=stdin EOF (peer closed) === === unhandled exception · 2026-08-19 12:23:47 === Traceback (most recent call last): File "<frozen runpy>", line 198, in _run_module_as_main File "<frozen runpy>", line 88, in _run_code File "tui_gateway/entry.py", line 490, in <module> main() File "tui_gateway/entry.py", line 465, in main if not handle_spurious_eof(_recovery_times, _log_exit): File "tui_gateway/_stdin_recovery.py", line 111, in handle_spurious_eof log_fn("stdin EOF (peer closed)") # type: ignore[operator] File "tui_gateway/entry.py", line 252, in _log_exit print(f"[gateway-exit] {reason}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True) BrokenPipeError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe ``` ## Root cause `_log_exit()` (`tui_gateway/entry.py`) guards its **disk** write but not its **stderr** write: ```python try: os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(_CRASH_LOG), exist_ok=True) with open(_CRASH_LOG, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(...) except Exception: pass print(f"[gateway-exit] {reason}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True) # <-- line 252, unguarded ``` The asymmetry is the bug. `_log_exit` is reached from `handle_spurious_eof()` (`_stdin_recovery.py:111` and `:100`) on the `return False` paths — i.e. *precisely when the peer has closed the pipe*. When the TUI parent tears down the child, stdin **and** stderr go away together, so the one function whose entire job is "record that the peer closed" writes to a descriptor the peer just closed. The exception escapes `_log_exit` → `handle_spurious_eof` → `main()` and terminates the interpreter as an unhandled exception. ## Reproduction 1. Run the TUI gateway (`hermes --tui`, or the desktop app). 2. Close it normally. 3. `tail ~/.hermes/logs/tui_gateway_crash.log` Every clean shutdown produces the `SIGHUP → SIGTERM → gateway exit (stdin EOF) → unhandled exception` sequence. Not a regression or a one-off — same failure on this host at `2026-06-01 15:07:38` under an older build, at the then-current line `entry.py:192` in the same `print(...)` statement. The surrounding `_stdin_recovery` refactor since then moved the line numbers but preserved the unguarded write. ## Expected A clean shutdown should not emit a traceback. `_log_exit` is a best-effort logger and should be total. ## Suggested fix Guard the stderr write the same way the file write already is: ```python try: print(f"[gateway-exit] {reason}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True) except (BrokenPipeError, ValueError, OSError): pass ``` (`ValueError` covers a closed-file `sys.stderr`; `OSError` is the `EPIPE`/`EBADF` superclass.) Worth auditing sibling best-effort log helpers on the shutdown path for the same unguarded-stderr shape. ## Environment - Hermes Agent v0.20.4 (2026.8.18), install method `git` - macOS (Darwin 27.0.0), arm64 - Python 3.11.15 (bundled `.hermes-runtime`) - Backend: local; source: TUI gateway child spawned by the TUI parent *(Paths in the traceback above are relative to the install root; absolute user paths redacted.)*

signal.title: `/reasoning off` hides thinking instead of disabling it, concealing that you are still paying for it
signal.text: ## Summary `/reasoning off` reads as "turn thinking off" but is the **display** toggle — it hides thinking from the transcript and leaves the model thinking (and billing) exactly as before. The actual disable is `/reasoning none`. The two spellings sit next to each other in the same command with no hint that they do unrelated things. ## Where Both the CLI and the gateway route `off` to the display branch: - `hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py` — `if arg in {"hide", "off"}` → `display.show_reasoning = False` - `gateway/slash_commands.py` — documented as `/reasoning hide|off Hide model reasoning from responses` The effort disable is a separate branch reached only by `none` (or `false` / `disabled`), which produces `{"enabled": False}`. ## Why it matters This is a silent, self-concealing failure. A user who wants to stop paying for thinking types the most natural word for it, the thinking text disappears from their screen, and they reasonably conclude it worked — while every turn still spends reasoning tokens. The one symptom that would reveal the mistake is the thing the command just hid. It also masks unrelated bugs in the same area. #90412 fixed a Nous profile bug where a real `{"enabled": false}` was dropped before it reached the Portal; that bug was reported from the desktop app, where the toggle sets a genuine disable. It went unreported from the terminal for ~3 months, and `/reasoning off` hiding the evidence is a plausible reason why. ## Related inconsistency `off` means *disabled* when it arrives as config rather than as a slash argument: YAML parses a bare `reasoning_effort: off` to boolean `False`, and `parse_reasoning_effort(False)` returns `{"enabled": False}`. So the same word means "hide it" as a command argument and "disable it" as a config value. (A *quoted* `reasoning_effort: "off"` is a third behavior — `parse_reasoning_effort` returns `None`, i.e. fall back to the default and keep thinking.) Worth noting `/reasoning off` is not documented anywhere in `website/docs`; the docs only show `/reasoning none` and `/reasoning hide`. ## Suggested fix Pick whichever fits the project's taste: 1. Drop `off` as an alias for `hide`, so it either disables or errors with a pointer to both spellings. 2. Keep it but warn: when a user types `/reasoning off`, hide the display **and** print a one-line note that thinking is still running and `/reasoning none` is what stops it. 3. Make `off` disable the effort (matching the config-value meaning) and leave `hide` as the display toggle. Option 2 is the least disruptive and kills the footgun outright.

signal.title: fix(desktop): Models/Providers settings no longer hang 20s when gh CLI is signed out
signal.text: ## Summary Desktop Settings → Model and Settings → Providers no longer take 20 seconds to load (and error with "Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms") when the gh CLI is installed but signed out. Root cause: `/api/model/options` probes Copilot auth via `gh auth token` four separate times per payload build. When gh has no credential store for the backend's HOME (fresh profile, desktop-spawned backend, CI), each probe blocks its full 5s subprocess timeout on keyring/D-Bus — 4×5s = 20s, past the renderer's 15s IPC budget, on **every** open of those pages. ## Changes - `hermes_cli/copilot_auth.py`: `_try_gh_cli_token()` now caches its result (hit or miss) for 5 minutes, with `_invalidate_gh_cli_token_cache()` for tests/re-auth; the uncached probe moved to `_probe_gh_cli_token()`. Probe subprocess gets `stdin=DEVNULL` and `GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1` / `GH_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1` so gh can never block on interactivity from a backend process. - Tests: 4 new cache-behavior tests (miss cached, hit cached, TTL expiry, explicit invalidation); existing homebrew-path test resets the cache. ## Validation | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `/api/model/options` cold (gh signed out) | 20.5s, every call | 5.3s (one bounded probe) | | `/api/model/options` warm | 20.5s | 0.03s | | Desktop Models/Providers page | error at 15s | loads | | Targeted tests (127) | — | all pass | Found during the full-desktop feature audit (Aug 19); reproduced live against a desktop-spawned worktree backend with a scratch HOME. ## Infographic ![Settings page 20-second hang fixed](https://files.catbox.moe/bppdw0.png)

signal.title: [Feature] Upgrade pre_api_request to a Transform hook — allow plugins to override model/provider/base_url per request
signal.text: # [Feature] Upgrade `pre_api_request` to a Transform hook — allow plugins to override model/provider/base_url per request ## Summary `pre_api_request` currently fires per provider attempt but is **observer-only** — its return value is ignored. I'd like it upgraded to a **Transform** hook (like `pre_transcription` and the `transform_*` family) so plugins can override request-time routing parameters (`model`, `provider`, `base_url`, `api_mode`, and optionally `extra_body`) before the LLM call is dispatched. ## Motivation ### 1. Peak/off-peak provider routing (cost savings) DeepSeek introduced peak/off-peak pricing (2026-08-17): off-peak is half of peak. For a cache-heavy agent workload (≈99% prompt-cache hit rate, tens of billions of cached input tokens/month), the cheapest channel differs by time of day: - **Off-peak** → DeepSeek direct API (cache-hit $0.007/M, the lowest cache price anywhere) - **Peak** → OpenRouter / third-party hosts (flat $0.07–$0.14/M output, no peak multiplier; cheaper than DeepSeek's peak $1.32/M output) An agent that runs 24/7 can save ~30–40% monthly by routing per-request: DeepSeek direct during off-peak hours, OpenRouter during peak hours. Today this is impossible without either (a) a fragile monkey-patch of `AIAgent._run_agent_loop()`, (b) an external LiteLLM proxy, or (c) a restart-requiring config flip. ### 2. Provider switch aligned with context compaction (zero-cost cache loss) Switching providers invalidates the prompt cache (a cache lives where it was written). Context compaction also invalidates it. Aligning a provider switch with a compaction event means the cache-miss cost is paid exactly once — the switch becomes effectively free. With a mutating `pre_api_request` hook, a plugin can detect that the previous turn compacted (e.g. via context-length delta or the compaction state exposed to plugins) and switch providers at that exact moment. ### 3. Task-type routing (existing community demand) The community plugin Hermes ARC / `topic_detect` (routes conversations by topic/domain) currently has to monkey-patch internals because no hook can cleanly change the model before a request (see #23739). ## Proposed change Make `pre_api_request` accept a return dict that overrides the outgoing request's routing parameters: ```python def on_pre_api_request(**kwargs): # kwargs: task_id, turn_id, api_request_id, session_id, model, provider, # base_url, api_mode, request_messages, approx_input_tokens, ... if _is_peak_hour() and _just_compacted(): return { "model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", "provider": "openrouter", "base_url": "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1", } return None # no change ctx.register_hook("pre_api_request", on_pre_api_request) ``` Semantics proposal (aligned with the existing hook taxonomy in `docs/plugins/hook-taxonomy.md`): - **Observer behavior preserved**: `None` / empty return → no change (backward compatible). - **Transform behavior added**: return a dict → fields are applied to the outgoing request, last-writer-wins per field in registration order (same model as `pre_transcription`). - Fields: `model`, `provider`, `base_url`, `api_mode`, and `extra_body` (for e.g. OpenRouter `session_id` sticky routing). - Errors in one callback must not break others (same isolation as existing hooks). ## Why this over a dedicated "compaction hook" A compaction hook answers *when* to switch; a mutating request hook answers *how*. The latter is the prerequisite — compaction is just one possible trigger among many (peak/off-peak, task type, queue pressure, quota depletion). A single transform-capable `pre_api_request` covers all of them, including cases nobody has imagined yet. ## Related issues - #23739 — allow `pre_llm_call` plugins to override model/provider at runtime (same root need, different hook) - #43237 — `transform_api_request` hook: plugin-accessible request middleware (this issue is essentially a narrower, concrete version of that proposal) - #72662 — DeepSeek peak-hour rate multiplier for cost tracking (adjacent: accurate cost accounting per peak/off-peak) ## Prior art in-tree `pre_transcription` (STT) is already a Transform hook that applies `prompt`, `language`, and `model` from a returned dict. The LLM request path is the notable gap. ## Acceptance criteria 1. A plugin can change `model`/`provider`/`base_url` per request via `pre_api_request` return value without touching core. 2. Returning `None` keeps current behavior byte-identical. 3. Documented in `website/docs/user-guide/features/hooks.md` with the new return contract. 4. Works for gateway sessions, CLI sessions, and subagents (delegated tasks).

signal.title: sessions import discards tool_use arguments and tool_result content
signal.text: `hermes_cli/foreign_sessions.py` discards tool call arguments and tool output when importing foreign sessions, so imported conversations lose the file contents, command output, and web fetches that make them intelligible. There are two affected sites. **Site 1 — `_flatten_blocks`, Claude Code (line ~117):** ```python elif btype == "tool_use": # Claude Code assistant block name = block.get("name") or "tool" parts.append(f"[ran tool: {name}]") elif btype == "tool_result": # Tool output echoed into a user message — not typed input. continue ``` Arguments are dropped and results are skipped entirely, so a session renders as a run of bare `[ran tool: Bash]` markers with no indication of what ran or what came back. **Site 2 — `parse_codex_session` (line ~266):** the same `[ran tool: {name}]` flattening, and `custom_tool_call_output` / `function_call_output` / `local_shell_call_output` payloads are never handled at all. ### Impact Measured on a local corpus of 26 Claude Code sessions: 3,045 `tool_use` arguments and 3,045 `tool_result` payloads discarded (~13.7M chars). Imported content was 429KB against 3.9MB of recoverable material — roughly a 9x loss. Sessions whose substance is tool work import as near-empty shells. Two related problems: 1. Sessions whose only content is tool activity fail with `No user/assistant conversation turns found` (line ~342) and are not imported at all. 2 of the 26 were lost this way. 2. Claude Code writes oversized tool results to `<session-dir>/tool-results/<id>.{json,txt}` and leaves a pointer in the JSONL. The importer stores the pointer rather than following it (13 such sidecars locally, 764KB). ### Suggested fix Render `tool_use` as `[tool: <name>] <arg-summary>` and `tool_result` as `[tool result]\n<content>`, preserving the plain user/assistant alternation the importer already enforces — no fabricated `tool_calls` structures. Guard the volume: replace binary payloads with a placeholder (a printable-character ratio test works well; Claude `view` on a PDF otherwise dumps megabytes of noise) and truncate long results with an explicit marker. I have a working patch against `fab8479` doing exactly this, including argument extraction that prefers `file_path` / `command` / `pattern` / `url` and falls back to compact JSON. Happy to open a PR if the approach looks right. Note `tests/hermes_cli/test_foreign_sessions.py` asserts the current behavior in two places (`[ran tool: Bash]` at :129, `[ran tool: shell]` at :148) plus four turn-count assertions, so those move with the fix. All 9 tests pass with both updated. ### Environment Hermes at `fab8479`, macOS 26.4, Python 3.11.

signal.title: feat(skills): add skill outcome evaluation and curator feedback
signal.text:
End-of-Turn Outcome Telemetry for Skills

Summary

Adds end-of-turn outcome telemetry — a third failure signal for skills.

Hermes already knew when the machinery broke and when the loop ended with text; this PR answers a question it never could: did the work actually hold up?

The answer is attributed to the skills that ran, flows into a per-skill sidecar, drives a needs_review curator flag, and is backed by a citation system — the judge can only blame a skill when it points at evidence that actually happened this turn.

Why

The curator's transitions (active → stale → archived) are driven purely by recency. A skill invoked constantly and failing constantly looks identical to one that works.

Outcome telemetry adds a failure dimension so unreliable skills get flagged instead of staying invisible.

Architecture

Three layers. Layers 0 and 1 are separately opt-in; Layer 2 is always-on, in-memory bookkeeping that the other two depend on.

Layer 1 — Mechanical Per-Skill Verifiers

tools/skill_verify.py

A skill's SKILL.md can declare metadata.hermes.verify:

  • run

  • optional applicability_check

  • timeout_seconds

After a turn that used the skill, the verifier subprocess runs and prints strict JSON:

{"success": true, "reason": "..."}

An applicability probe that exits non-zero yields SKIP — recorded as nothing, never a fake pass.

A turn-wide budget (total_verify_budget_seconds, default 60s) caps all verifier subprocesses.

Layer 0 — End-of-Turn Outcome Judge

agent/turn_outcome.py

After finalization, an auxiliary model judge answers:

Did the work hold up, not merely did the loop end?

It returns:

{ "task_succeeded": true, "confidence": 0.95, "failure_points": [], "reason": "..." }

The judge runs only when:

  • a verifier FAILED;

  • a used skill had no verifier (unverified residue — the common case); or

  • run: always is configured.

Down-Only, Dumb-Recorder Attribution

The attribution system deliberately only allows evidence to move outcomes downward:

  • A mechanical verifier FAIL is foreclosed: it is recorded, and no auxiliary judgment can overturn it.

  • On a confident evaluation success, a skill that ran unverified records NEUTRAL — a sample that slides the recovery window but never claims success.

  • When a mechanical FAIL is present, the eval's additional failure_points are ignored — a low-context judge cannot pin blame on an unrelated skill.

  • Verdicts are best-effort — a failure in the evaluation path never breaks the turn.

Recorder-Side Rejection — Blame Must Cite Evidence

Previously, the judge blamed skills using bare names. The recorder wrote those with the same sidecar status as a mechanical verifier's True/False — a conclusion stored as if it were a fact, with nothing downstream able to distinguish the two.

This closes that gap.

failure_points is now a citation:

[ { "skill": "<name>", "evidence": [1, 3] } ]

The IDs point at a numbered evidence catalog built from this turn's real artifacts:

  • mechanical verifier verdicts;

  • tool errors, newly enumerated in finalize_turn with their tool names;

  • failed file mutations.

The recorder validates every citation mechanically before writing a False:

  • A citation to a verifier FAIL for the exact skill is hard — the citation itself is the evidence, and the failure lands regardless of confidence.

  • A citation to tool-error/file-mutation evidence, or no citation (legacy bare name), is gated — it remains confidence-gated because the skill attribution is judge-attributed.

  • Fabricated IDs, cited PASS results, and another skill's FAIL are rejected — the outcome is recorded as NEUTRAL, with the judge's reason preserved, never as a hard False.

  • Legacy bare-name failure_points still parse and behave exactly as before (confidence-gated), preserving backward compatibility.

Layer 2 — Per-Turn Skill Attribution

tools/skill_usage.py + agent/turn_context.py

The dumb recorder answers:

Which skills actually ran this turn?

At turn start, arm_turn_skill_accumulator points a ContextVar at the agent's _turn_used_skills.

The accumulator is:

  • written through the single bump_use() chokepoint;

  • read from the instance, so a subagent cannot pollute the parent's attribution;

  • disarmed at turn end, so out-of-turn bump_use() calls — preloads, cron, shared gateway threads — stop writing into a dead set.

Layer 2 is ungated, always-on bookkeeping. It is the reason neither a mechanical failure nor an eval-blamed skill can be pinned to a skill the turn never touched.

Declaring Is Not Consent — The Trust Boundary

A skill author may declare a verifier, but only the user grants permission to run it via:

hermes skills verify <name>

or:

/skills verify <name> [--disable]

Opt-in is gated by is_verify_optin_eligible():

Skill type | Eligible -- | -- Agent-created / curator-managed | Always Bundled built-ins | Only when curator.prune_builtins is enabled Hub-installed, external, protected, unmanaged | Never

Enabling is gated; disabling is always allowed. Consent therefore remains revocable even if a skill later drifts into ineligibility.

Sidecar Telemetry

tools/skill_usage.py

bump_outcome() records outcomes in a bounded window of the last 20 samples:

  • recent_outcomes

  • recent_outcome_reasons

  • failure_rate()

The needs_review flag:

  • turns on at ≥50% failures with ≥4 samples;

  • turns off on recovery;

  • clears when the skill is archived.

Curator Integration

agent/curator.py

needs_review skills are:

  • counted during automatic transitions;

  • promoted to priority candidates in the LLM review pass;

  • surfaced through:

hermes curator status

with:

needs review (N): ...

Surface

CLI

hermes skills list gains a Verify column, computed in a single pass while mirroring the eligibility rule.

Auxiliary Task

The outcome auxiliary task is registered in:

  • the CLI picker;

  • the web REST allowlist;

  • both TSX mirror arrays.

It is configurable under:

hermes model → auxiliary

Configuration

Configuration lives under auxiliary.outcome:

auxiliary: outcome: enabled: false run: auto provider: ... model: ... max_tokens: ... total_verify_budget_seconds: 60

Disabled means zero cost beyond a configuration read.

Validation

119 unit tests across:

  • test_turn_outcome.py

  • test_turn_outcome_finalize_e2e.py

  • test_turn_finalizer_count_tool_errors.py

  • test_skill_usage.py

  • test_skill_verify.py

  • test_curator_status.py

All tests are green.

signal.title: fix(windows): resolve memory provider command shims
signal.text:
## Summary Fix native-Windows memory-provider dependency checks for CLI tools installed through npm shims such as ByteRover's `brv.cmd`. On Windows, the dashboard and `hermes memory setup` were passing a bare command like `brv` directly to `subprocess.run([...])`. Python ultimately calls `CreateProcessW`, which does not perform PATHEXT resolution for this argv form, so a valid npm-installed CLI could fail with: ```text FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified ``` This caused the Plugins page to report ByteRover as missing even while: ```text where.exe brv C:
vm4w
odejs rv C:
vm4w
odejs rv.cmd brv --version byterover-cli/3.16.1 win32-x64 node-v22.23.2 hermes memory status Plugin: installed Status: available ``` ## Fix - split external dependency check commands with Windows-aware `shlex` behavior - resolve argv[0] with `shutil.which()` on Windows before calling `subprocess.run` - apply the same fix to: - CLI memory-provider setup - dashboard dependency-installed checks - dashboard pre-install checks - dashboard post-install verification - preserve the existing behavior when the executable cannot be resolved For an npm-installed ByteRover CLI this turns: ```text brv --version ``` into an argv beginning with the actual launcher, e.g.: ```text C:
vm4w
odejs rv.CMD ``` ## Regression coverage Adds tests covering: - `.cmd` shim resolution in the dashboard path - unresolved-command fallback behavior - `.cmd` shim resolution in the CLI memory setup path The tests mock Windows behavior so they can run on non-Windows CI as well. ## Reproduction / validation Reproduced on native Windows 11 with NVM for Windows, Node 22.23.2, and `byterover-cli` 3.16.1. Before the fix, the Plugins page returned `missing brv` / `[WinError 2]`; after resolving the shim path and restarting the dashboard, ByteRover showed `ready` and `active` and the dependency warning disappeared. This PR is intentionally scoped to executable resolution. The ByteRover manifest's Unix-oriented install command is a separate portability concern.

signal.title: feat(desktop): Space stages clarify choices from the keyboard
signal.text: ## Summary The desktop clarify card can now be driven fully from the keyboard: **Space stages/toggles the highlighted choice without submitting**, matching the standard option-list convention. Enter stays the confirm key. Inspired by Factory Droid v0.199 ("Question prompt keyboard controls" — answers pickable with Space or number keys). Hermes already had arrow/letter/number navigation on the clarify card; Space was the gap — it did nothing on the card and fell through to the global type-to-focus listener, which yanked focus into the composer with a leading space, silently killing the staged selection. ## Changes - `clarify-tool.tsx`: Space stages the highlighted choice (single-select) or toggles it (multi-select) without submitting; on the "Other" row it focuses the free-text field. - `composer-focus-keys.ts`: a live clarify card now owns the Space key (`clarifyCardOwnsKey`) so type-to-focus yields it — a real composer message never starts with a leading space, so this costs nothing. - Tests: 3 new clarify-tool cases (stage-then-confirm, multi-select toggle, Other-row focus) + updated the composer-focus-keys ownership pin. ## Validation | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Space on highlighted choice | focus jumps to composer, " " typed | choice staged, card keeps focus | | Space on multi-select choice | same composer steal | toggles the choice in the staged set | | `vitest run` clarify-tool + composer-focus-keys | 41 tests | 44/44 pass | Source: [Droid v0.199 release notes](https://docs.factory.ai/changelog/release-notes) (Aug 18, 2026). Their mechanism: Space/number pick answers, Tab moves between questions. Our adaptation: Space maps onto Hermes' existing stage-then-confirm model (Droid picks immediately; we deliberately keep Enter as the explicit confirm, consistent with the card's Continue button). Tab-between-questions was not ported — the batch card stages all questions in one form and native Tab traversal already walks its fields. ## Infographic ![Space stages your choice — keyboard controls for clarify cards](https://files.catbox.moe/70rzd3.png)

signal.title: Desktop: messages sent to a WS-detached session after reconnect are silently dropped (no resume, no error)
signal.text: ## Summary After a transient WebSocket disconnect (laptop sleep / network blip — not a crash), messages sent **into an already-open session** are silently dropped: the client shows them as sent, but they never reach the backend (no `tui prompt accepted` in `gui.log`, no new row in the `messages` table), and **no error is surfaced to the user**. The session looks alive in the UI but is effectively dead. Distinct from #87920 (session view goes stale, but *sending a message recovers* via rebind) and #77127 (TOCTOU race between teardown and `session.resume`): here the resume/rebind path is **never triggered at all**, so sending a message does not recover the session — it disappears. ## Environment - Hermes Agent v0.20.3 (2026.8.16.2), git install - macOS (Desktop app, local backend via `hermes serve`) - Python 3.11.15 ## Timeline (from logs) | Time (local) | Event | |---|---| | 02:40:25 | WS closed: `client_disconnect(code=1006)`, `detached_sessions=3` | | 02:40:26 | WS reconnects (**1 s later — well inside the 20 s orphan-reap grace window**) | | — | No `session.resume` is re-issued for the previously open sessions after reconnect | | +20 s | Orphan reaper tears down the detached in-memory sessions (DB rows survive) | | hours later | User sends messages into the old session → **never reach backend**, no `prompt accepted` log, no DB row, no UI error | ## Log evidence (sanitized — localhost only) ``` 2026-08-19 02:40:25,692 INFO tui_gateway.ws: ws closed peer=127.0.0.1:57686 reason=client_disconnect(code=1006,reason=) messages=872 parse_errors=0 dispatch_crashes=0 send_failures=0 reaped_sessions=0 detached_sessions=3 2026-08-19 02:40:26,550 INFO tui_gateway.ws: ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:61244 ``` After the reconnect there are **zero** `session.resume` / `tui prompt accepted` records for the detached sessions (checked `gui.log`), and the session's last DB message stays at the pre-disconnect timestamp — confirming the later sends never arrived. ## Root cause (source reading) - `tui_gateway/ws.py:429-476` — WS teardown detaches non-`close_on_disconnect` sessions and hands them to the grace-windowed orphan reaper. - `tui_gateway/server.py:1125-1163` (`_schedule_ws_orphan_reap`) — 20 s grace; a reconnect + `session.resume` that re-binds a live transport cancels the reap (comment: *"a quick reconnect / session.resume that re-binds a live transport cancels the reap"*). - The desktop client reconnects the WS transport but does **not** re-issue `session.resume` for sessions that were open before the disconnect — resume is only triggered on route change / explicit session selection (`use-route-resume.ts`, `use-prompt-actions/submit.ts`). The UI store still believes the session is live, so `submit.ts` takes the fast path (existing runtime id) instead of the resume path → the prompt is sent to a session the backend already reaped → silently dropped. ## Suggested fix directions 1. On WS reconnect, desktop should re-resume the sessions that were attached before the disconnect (or at minimum detect a dead runtime on submit and fall back to `session.resume`). 2. Surface a user-visible error/notice when a send fails to reach a live session instead of dropping it silently. 3. Backend could return a distinguishable error when a prompt targets a reaped/unknown runtime session. ## Related issues - #87920 — GUI session view goes stale on WS reconnect (different symptom: sending a message recovers the view) - #77127 — WS disconnect teardown race can close/orphan a session reconnected via `session.resume` - #53374 — Desktop creates new session after sleep (WS disconnect, session context lost)

signal.title: [Setup]: install domain hermes-agent.nousresearch.com serving invalid TLS certificate (Let's Encrypt cert expired 2026-08-18) — Quick Install one-liner fails
signal.text: ### What happened The Quick Install one-liner from the README fails for all new users because `hermes-agent.nousresearch.com` is serving an invalid TLS certificate: ``` $ curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate ``` ### Diagnosis The server is presenting a certificate from an unknown private issuer instead of a publicly trusted one: ``` $ echo | openssl s_client -connect hermes-agent.nousresearch.com:443 -servername hermes-agent.nousresearch.com 0 s:/O=NetAlerts/CN=hermes-agent.nousresearch.com i:/O=NetAlerts/CN=NetAlerts Services Verify return code: 21 (unable to verify the first certificate) ``` Certificate Transparency history (crt.sh) shows the domain's Let's Encrypt R13 certificate **expired 2026-08-18** (yesterday as of filing). A newer Let's Encrypt YR2 certificate was issued 2026-07-21 (valid to 2026-10-19) but does not appear to be deployed. The host (45.54.28.16, NetActuate anycast) now serves what looks like a hosting-appliance fallback cert ("NetAlerts"). Verified from two independent networks, and DNS answers are consistent across Cloudflare/Google resolvers, so this is server-side, not client-side. ### Impact - `curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash` fails (macOS, and presumably all platforms) - `iex (irm https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.ps1)` presumably fails the same way - Docs links (`hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/...`) fail with TLS errors - Risk that frustrated new users bypass verification with `curl -k`, which this incident shows is exactly the wrong habit to teach ### Workaround that worked Fetching the same script from the repo and running it locally: ``` curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/scripts/install.sh -o hermes-install.sh bash hermes-install.sh ``` ### Suggested fix Deploy the already-issued YR2 certificate (or re-issue) on the web host serving `hermes-agent.nousresearch.com`.

signal.title: feat(relay)!: initialize static/dynamic plugins via native integration, remove opt-in plugin
signal.text: > [!WARNING] > **Breaking change — migration is required for existing NeMo Relay plugin users.** > > This PR removes the bundled Hermes `observability/nemo_relay` plugin and moves > `plugin.initialize()` lifecycle ownership into the core `RelayRuntime`. Before > upgrading, remove `observability/nemo_relay` (or the legacy `nemo_relay` alias) > from `plugins.enabled` and move exporter/middleware configuration into a Relay > `plugins.toml` selected with `HERMES_NEMO_RELAY_PLUGINS_TOML`. > > Legacy `HERMES_NEMO_RELAY_ATOF_*` and `HERMES_NEMO_RELAY_ATIF_*` variables no > longer activate exporters. When `HERMES_NEMO_RELAY_PLUGINS_TOML` is unset, > Hermes does not initialize Relay plugins and Relay performs no plugin discovery > or configuration layering. When it points to a valid file, Relay performs its > normal static discovery/layering and Hermes owns the resulting process-global > activation. If another host already has an active Relay plugin configuration, > Hermes leaves it unchanged and disables Hermes-managed Relay middleware rather > than replacing it. > > Relay plugin policy is a process boundary. The selected static configuration, > discovered layers, middleware, exporters, guardrails, and dynamic plugins apply > to every profile hosted by that Hermes process. ATIF keeps top-level Agent > trajectories separate, while ATOF and other global subscribers observe events > from every hosted profile. Run profiles in separate Hermes processes when they > require different trust levels, plugin credentials, exporter destinations, or > guardrail policies. > > Upgrade safeguards in this PR migrate stale `plugins.enabled` entries out of > config v35, warn through `hermes doctor` and runtime diagnostics, and reject > user-installed copies of the removed plugin identity. ## What does this PR do? This PR adds explicitly configured NeMo Relay plugin activation to Hermes's native in-process Relay runtime and removes the overlapping bundled `observability/nemo_relay` Hermes plugin. The native SDK integrations remain in place: Hermes provides Relay session, turn, task, and manual scopes, shared-metrics lifecycle events, and SDK-managed LLM/tool adapter paths independently of whether plugin activation is enabled. The native runtime calls neither `nemo_relay.plugin.initialize(...)` nor `initialize_with_dynamic_plugins(...)` unless `HERMES_NEMO_RELAY_PLUGINS_TOML` is set to a non-empty path and the selected file loads successfully. With the variable unset, native Relay instrumentation continues normally, but Hermes does not activate Relay middleware, exporters, dynamic plugins, or ambient `plugins.toml` discovery. When explicitly enabled and the selected file loads successfully, Hermes passes its static components to Relay as a programmatic overlay. Relay performs its normal static `plugins.toml` discovery and layering, with the selected static configuration taking precedence. Hermes delegates canonical `[[plugins.dynamic]]` manifest resolution and validation to Relay 0.7.1 before opening the first Relay session scope; dynamic records are loaded from the selected file only. The unreleased Hermes-specific top-level `[[dynamic_plugins]]` format and parser have been removed. If the selected file is missing, unreadable, malformed, contains an invalid dynamic declaration, or Relay rejects it, Hermes reports the failure and continues without native plugin activation. Because Hermes does not invoke Relay's initializer on that failure path, it does not fall back to ambient discovery. Initialization and activation are process-wide. The first hosted profile's plugin decision is represented explicitly as disabled, active, foreign, or failed, and additional profile-scoped Hermes hosts share that decision rather than retrying or selecting a different policy. Successful initialization emits `Relay plugins are active process-wide and apply to all profiles hosted by this Hermes process.` exactly once. After the final host stops admitting work and active operations drain, Hermes closes sessions, flushes subscribers/exporters, and clears or closes the Relay plugin activation. Per-session close does not perform a global subscriber flush, avoiding a concurrent-session event-loop deadlock. Profile scopes preserve causal isolation inside that shared policy. ATIF produces separate trajectories for separate top-level Agent scopes, while ATOF and other global subscribers observe activity from every hosted profile. Static and dynamic middleware applies to calls from every profile, and worker invocations retain the invoking profile's Relay scope stack. Profiles requiring different trust, plugin credentials, exporter destinations, or guardrail policies must run in separate Hermes processes. Removing `plugins/observability/nemo_relay` establishes a single lifecycle owner for Relay configuration. Deployments that previously enabled that Hermes plugin should remove it from their enabled-plugin configuration and express middleware/exporter configuration in the TOML selected by `HERMES_NEMO_RELAY_PLUGINS_TOML`. Hermes-native shared metrics do not require the removed plugin. This PR relies on the Relay `>=0.7.1,<0.8` requirement already present on `main`; it does not modify `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock`. Because Relay 0.7.1 is the minimum supported version, the native runtime calls `initialize`, `initialize_with_dynamic_plugins`, `load_dynamic_plugin_activation_specs`, `flush_async`, and `clear_async` directly. It retains fail-open handling for operational failures, but no longer carries Relay 0.6-era missing-method checks or synchronous cleanup fallbacks. ## Why remove `observability/nemo_relay`? The bundled Hermes plugin and the native runtime were two independent owners of the same process-global Relay state. If both were enabled, each could initialize Relay from its own configuration and register middleware, subscribers, exporters, or dynamic plugins. That made behavior dependent on startup order and allowed several invalid or buggy configurations: - the same exporter or subscriber could be installed twice, producing duplicate events, traces, or trajectory output; - middleware could wrap the same Hermes LLM or tool operation more than once; - one integration could replace or clear configuration owned by the other; - one integration could flush subscribers or close dynamic-plugin activation while another Hermes host or managed operation was still using it; - separate configuration paths could disagree about which components were active, making failures difficult to diagnose. The native integration now provides the complete supported path: Hermes owns session and operation context, while Relay owns plugin parsing, activation, exporter/subscriber registration, and dynamic-plugin lifecycle. Removing the overlapping Hermes plugin gives that process-global state one owner and one teardown boundary. It does **not** remove Relay observability or shared metrics; deployments configure those components in the `plugins.toml` selected by `HERMES_NEMO_RELAY_PLUGINS_TOML`. ## Related Issue Relates to [NVIDIA/NeMo-Relay#694](https://github.com/NVIDIA/NeMo-Relay/pull/694) ## Type of Change - [x] ⚠️ Breaking change (requires migration from `observability/nemo_relay` to core `RelayRuntime` ownership) - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [x] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [x] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - Relay cutover safeguards - migrate config v35 by removing only the legacy Relay identities from `plugins.enabled`; - warn on stale plugin keys and ignored legacy ATOF/ATIF exporter variables; - reject user/entry-point copies of the removed plugin identity; - leave a pre-existing foreign process-global Relay configuration unchanged instead of replacing it. - `agent/relay_runtime.py` - gates native Relay plugin initialization on an explicit `HERMES_NEMO_RELAY_PLUGINS_TOML` path; - enables Relay's normal static discovery and layering only after the selected TOML loads successfully; - layers selected static components over discovered configuration and loads canonical `[[plugins.dynamic]]` records from the selected file only; - rejects the unreleased Hermes-specific `[[dynamic_plugins]]` format instead of maintaining a second parser; - uses the required Relay 0.7.1 plugin and subscriber APIs directly, without obsolete capability checks or synchronous cleanup fallbacks; - fails open without invoking Relay initialization or falling back to ambient discovery when the selected file is invalid; - owns activation and final cleanup process-wide; - records the first hosted profile's process decision with an explicit state enum and shares it with later hosts; - emits one process-wide diagnostic only after plugin initialization completes successfully; - drains deferred managed operations before teardown and avoids per-session global subscriber flushes. - `agent/relay_llm.py` - preserves managed-operation ownership through stream completion and cleanup; - uses canonical Relay operation names and keeps client-only timeouts off provider wire payloads; - safely handles completed-response and streaming provider paths. - `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` and `agent/transports/chat_completions.py` - tolerate sparse SDK response and stream-delta objects when optional fields are absent. - `plugins/observability/nemo_relay/` - removed to prevent duplicate initialization, activation, exporter, and teardown ownership; - native shared metrics and Relay plugin activation remain available through core. - Documentation and `scripts/toolperf_abeval` - migrate references and exporter setup to the Hermes-native TOML path. - Tests - cover explicit configuration gating, initialization ordering, canonical dynamic loading, legacy-format rejection, static/dynamic ownership, exporter output, stream cleanup, and concurrent shutdown; - prove static and dynamic middleware reaches two profile hosts with distinct Relay scope stacks; - prove ATOF observes two profiles while ATIF keeps their top-level Agent trajectories separate; - remove tests for the deleted legacy integration. ## How to Test ```sh scripts/run_tests.sh \ tests/agent/test_relay_runtime_plugins.py \ tests/agent/test_relay_llm.py \ tests/agent/test_relay_tools.py \ tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_cmd_enable_disable_nested.py \ tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_cmd_category_discovery.py \ tests/hermes_cli/test_relay_shared_metrics_runtime.py \ tests/hermes_cli/test_relay_shared_metrics.py uv run ruff check \ hermes_cli/plugins_cmd.py \ scripts/toolperf_abeval/ab_eval.py \ tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_cmd_enable_disable_nested.py uv lock --check ``` Cutover guard validation: `166 passed` across the full config, doctor, and plugin-manager suites, plus `31 passed` in the focused Relay ownership/migration suite. Ruff and whitespace checks passed. Focused validation after removing the legacy plugin: `224 passed`. The final canonical configuration and Relay 0.7.1 API tightening was additionally validated with `217 passed` across the native Relay, nested-execution, shared-metrics, and smoke suites. It introduces a public backend contract and registry-backed lifecycle while preserving the behavior of the existing built-in backends. Third-party plugins can register terminal backends through the standard `PluginContext` without adding backend-specific dispatch logic to `terminal_tool`. The implementation centralizes backend discovery, availability checks, construction, diagnostics, and lifecycle management. Terminal, file, code-execution, and process tools resolve the selected backend through the same registry and environment abstractions, ensuring that plugin-provided backends receive the same cwd, filesystem, process, timeout, and cleanup behavior as built-in backends. This approach: - reuses the existing plugin discovery and `plugins.enabled` trust boundary; - avoids a separate entry-point group or backend-specific plugin loader; - removes hard-coded built-in dispatch from runtime paths; - keeps backend inventories and diagnostics derived from the registry; - preserves existing built-in backend behavior and configuration compatibility. ## Related Issue Related work: - [NousResearch/hermes-agent#56900](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/56900) — the original coder backend PR proposed before the pluggable backend architecture. - signal.title: fix(compression): attribute auxiliary failures to the actual wire route
signal.text: ## Summary When auxiliary context compression fails, Hermes can surface the main model's provider, model, and endpoint instead of the route that actually failed. This sends users to troubleshoot a healthy main endpoint and becomes especially misleading when `provider: auto`, retries, or a runtime fallback changes the physical request route. ## Root Cause The compressor is initialized with the main model runtime fields, while the auxiliary route is resolved later inside `call_llm()`. The previous diagnostic therefore could not reliably identify the auxiliary request. An initial route callback was also insufficient because it ran only once: it could retain `Provider: auto` or the first client after a retry or fallback had already moved the request elsewhere. ## Changes - `agent/auxiliary_client.py` - Carry an optional route callback in the per-call relay context. - Invoke it immediately before every physical synchronous wire attempt, including the initial call, same-provider retries, client rebuilds, credential rotation, and runtime fallback candidates. - Report a concrete provider derived from the actual client endpoint when configuration resolution returns `auto`. Endpoints whose provider cannot be inferred from the wire URL report `custom` — this means "auto-selected HTTP client with an unrecognized endpoint", not a provider name, so dashboards/logs should not read it as one. - Report the final request model and query-stripped `client.base_url`, so later attempts replace earlier route snapshots without exposing query credentials. The relay context's `main_runtime.base_url` copy is also stored query-stripped for the same reason. - `agent/context_compressor.py` - Record the latest physical auxiliary route for the current summary attempt. - Classify the current attempt as `auth`, `network`, or `other` without reusing a stale sticky cooldown classification. - `agent/conversation_compression.py` - Emit the diagnostic only from the centralized compression-abort path, after the auxiliary attempt has completed. - Use the terminating route snapshot and gateway-visible wording. - `tests/agent/test_compression_auth_error_attribution.py` - Cover the real `call_llm()` orchestration for `provider: auto`, exact provider/model/endpoint reporting, query-string redaction, and a primary-to-fallback terminal failure. - Retain end-to-end coverage from `ContextCompressor` through the compression-abort diagnostic, including stale-classification and gateway visibility cases. ## Validation ```text scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_compression_auth_error_attribution.py tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client.py tests/agent/test_auxiliary_relay.py tests/agent/test_context_compressor.py tests/gateway/test_telegram_noise_filter.py -q ``` - 404 focused tests passed. - `python3 -m py_compile` passed for the modified Python files. - `git diff --check` passed. - Tested on macOS 26.5. Closes #72636
