signal.title: fix(state): stop the unbounded state.db repair loop (salvage of #88224)
signal.text: ## Summary A malformed-**schema** `state.db` now stops repairing itself after 3 failed attempts instead of looping forever — and the pre-repair forensic copy is a real copy, not a partially-written staging file. Salvage of #88224 by @jirathip-k, cherry-picked to preserve authorship, plus two data-integrity fixes found in review. ## Why the loop never terminated (@jirathip-k's diagnosis, verbatim in commits 1–2) #86867 shipped an attempt ledger and a backup retention cap for exactly this shape of failure. Both were present and both were structurally dead, because they keyed on `size:mtime_ns`. That key assumes "size+mtime is stable for a file nothing can successfully write to" — true for the b-tree page damage of #86867, false for the malformed-**schema** class: the DB still opens and accepts writes (only `sqlite_master` is unreadable), so live writers, WAL checkpoints and the in-place repair strategies themselves all move mtime between passes. Every pass looked like a brand-new file, so the counter reset to 1 forever and the dedupe never matched — a fresh ~98MB copy every ~10s. Reproduced against the unpatched tree: ``` === A: stable mtime (the assumption #86867 was tested under) === pass 1..3: failed_attempts=1,2,3 pass 4: BLOCKED by ledger (guard held) === B: mtime moves between passes (this incident) === pass 1..8: failed_attempts=1 (every pass) NEVER BLOCKED ``` ## Changes **Commits 1–2 — @jirathip-k** (unmodified) - `hermes_state.py`: fingerprint on content (size + sha256 of the first/last 64KB) for both the ledger and the backup dedupe; atomic staged backup; proportional free-space guard (`max(256MiB, 2% of volume)` rather than a flat multi-GB floor that would refuse backups on small container/VM volumes and, because refusal is the #69603 hard stop, silently convert "repair loops" into "repair never runs"). - `tests/test_state_db_repair_loop_mtime.py`: 14 tests. **Commit 3 — lock safety (review finding)** The content fingerprint takes a raw descriptor, and `close()` on **any** descriptor cancels every POSIX advisory lock the process holds on that file ([sqlite.org](https://sqlite.org/howtocorrupt.html#_posix_advisory_locks_canceled_by_a_separate_thread_doing_close_)). `hermes_cli/sqlite_safe_read.py` rule 1 is "never `open()` a database file that may have live connections in this process". `_backup_db_file` guards this with `has_live_connection()`, but the exhaustion probe at `hermes_state.py:2426` runs *before* that guard — and `_backup_db_file`'s own docstring notes the repair path is entered by one SessionDB while the gateway holds others. E2E, real `repair_state_db_schema()`, `journal_mode=DELETE`, gateway mid-turn write, peer in a subprocess: | | before repair | after repair | holder `COMMIT` | |---|---|---|---| | #88224 as-is | peer BLOCKED | peer **STOLE the write lock** | `disk I/O error` | | this PR | peer BLOCKED | peer BLOCKED | ok | WAL is immune (it coordinates through `-shm`), but DELETE is what Hermes falls back to on NFS/SMB/FUSE/ZFS (`hermes_state.py:649`) and on SQLite builds vulnerable to the WAL-reset bug (`:1417`) — a real deployment shape, which is why `_log_wal_fallback_once` is an ERROR. Fix: run the read under `offline_file_access`, falling back to `size:mtime_ns` when a connection is live. Returning `None` there would have been worse than the bug — it reads as "not exhausted" and restores the unbounded loop. The content key stays load-bearing on the offline repair path, the only path where surgery actually runs. Also fails the free-space guard **closed**: a nearly-full volume is exactly where `statvfs` is likeliest to fail, and proceeding is the multi-GB copy that finishes off the disk. **Commit 5 — never let a peer connection reset the repair budget (self-review finding)** Commit 3's `size:mtime_ns` fallback **reintroduced this PR's own bug by a different route**. The ledger compares keys for *equality*, and the two keys have different *shapes*, so a gateway peer connecting between passes flipped the shape and the counter reset to 1 every time: ``` pass 1 [offline] attempts=1 fp=8192:58c7924f0fba... pass 2 [LIVE ] attempts=1 fp=8192:1786972039271402096 pass 3 [offline] attempts=1 fp=8192:58c7924f0fba... -> never terminates ``` Now returns `None`, with both ledger helpers taught to cope: the exhaustion probe falls back to the recorded key's **size prefix** (the one component both shapes share and that needs no raw read) instead of reading as "not exhausted", and the recorder keeps the key already on record and still increments instead of dropping the pass. Result: `attempts=1,2,3` then BLOCKED at pass 4 regardless of liveness alternation. Intra-pass flips were already safe — the probe and the record see the same liveness within one `repair_state_db_schema` call; it was the cross-pass change that desynced. **Commit 6 — exclude SQLite's commit counters from the fingerprint (self-review finding)** The content sample started at byte 0, so it covered the header's file change counter (bytes 24-27) and version-valid-for (92-95). In DELETE mode a commit writes the main file directly and bumps both — and a malformed-schema DB still accepts writes, which is this PR's whole premise. So **any ordinary session write between passes re-keyed the ledger and the fix was defeated exactly like the original mtime bug**: ``` DELETE, 18MB db, one peer UPDATE between passes before: pass 1..6 -> attempts=1 every pass, never exhausted after: pass 1..3 -> attempts=1,2,3; pass 4 -> BLOCKED ``` Invisible on a WAL host (commits land in `-wal`; the main header only moves on checkpoint) and reproducible on every NFS/SMB/FUSE/ZFS or WAL-reset-vulnerable host — i.e. precisely the deployments commit 3 was written for. Masked the two volatile ranges out of the sample; page 1's `sqlite_master` b-tree sits after byte 100 and stays in, so schema rewrite / index rebuild / VACUUM / truncation all still reset the budget while a bare `utime` and an ordinary commit do not. **Commit 7 — include the rollback journal in the forensic backup (review finding)** The copy took only `-wal`/`-shm`. In DELETE mode a hot `<db>-journal` exists whenever a transaction was open, and it is what rolls the damaged bytes back to a consistent state — a forensic copy without it can't be recovered by hand, defeating the point of taking it before destructive surgery. Added `_DB_SIDECAR_SUFFIXES = ("-wal", "-shm", "-journal")` and used it at the four sites that must agree: disk-guard sizing, the staging copy, the backup-count exclusion (so a copied journal isn't itself counted as a backup), and prune (which otherwise leaks one journal per pruned backup, quietly defeating the retention cap). Matches the spelling `hermes_cli/session_recovery.py:61` already uses. **Commit 4 — staging must not pose as a forensic copy (review finding)** Staging was named `<db>.malformed-backup-<stamp>.incomplete`, which still matches the prefix `_existing_malformed_backups` selects on (it excludes only `-wal`/`-shm`). So it was counted as a backup, and it sorts **newest** (`.incomplete` > the bare stamp), meaning prune's keep-3-newest slice retained partials and deleted intact copies — the exact inversion the staging change was meant to prevent. Worse: the dedupe ran *before* the sweep, and a staging file orphaned by a kill mid-copy is a byte-identical copy of the damaged DB, so its fingerprint matches and it was returned as the official `backup_path`. Repair then passed the #69603 hard-stop gate and ran destructive surgery believing a forensic copy existed — and the next pass's sweep deleted that very file. ``` before backup_path = ...malformed-backup-<stamp>.incomplete (staging!) pass-1 forensic copy deleted by the next sweep after backup_path = ...malformed-backup-<stamp> (real copy) debris swept, pass-1 forensic copy preserved ``` Fix: stage outside the prefix (`<db>.backup-staging-<stamp>`) and sweep before the dedupe. The sweep also matches the old `.incomplete` spelling so a host that ran the earlier build doesn't keep prefix-matching debris that sorts newest and survives prune forever. ## Validation | | result | |---|---| | `test_state_db_repair_loop_mtime.py` | 26 passed (14 theirs + 12 added) | | `test_state_db_repair_loop_cap.py` (#86867) | 9 passed — no regression | | `test_state_db_malformed_repair.py` | 16 passed | | `test_hermes_state.py` + `test_doctor_journal_modes.py` | 273 passed, 2 skipped | | ruff | clean | | `ty` | no new diagnostics vs `origin/main` (base has 131 pre-existing; this PR adds none) | Mutation-checked, one revert at a time: dropping the `offline_file_access` guard fails both lock-safety tests; restoring the in-prefix staging name fails both staging tests; restoring `except OSError: pass` fails the fail-closed test; restoring the `size:mtime_ns` fallback **or** making the recorder drop a `None`-fingerprint pass fails the budget-alternation test. Against pre-PR `hermes_state.py`, 14 of 26 fail. Regression tests added (7): fingerprint takes no raw fd while a connection is live; a live connection keeps its write lock across a repair pass (peer in a subprocess — a same-process peer shares lock ownership and makes the test vacuous); staging name is outside the backup prefix (observes the real staging path rather than hardcoding it); orphaned staging is never returned as `backup_path`; backup refused when free space can't be determined; budget exhausts when liveness alternates across passes; fingerprint returns `None` rather than a second key shape. ## Notes - The 64KB head sample is sufficient: SQLite bumps the change-counter at **byte 27** of page 1 on every write (verified — a middle-row UPDATE on a 27MB DB changed the head sample), so a partially-successful repair can't leave head+tail+size identical. - Test cost addressed rather than deferred: the two guard tests that allocated 450MB of `os.urandom` now use sparse `truncate` (both only ever read `st_size`), and the new larger-than-sample fixtures use 600 rows rather than 40k. File runtime 127s → 35s. - The trigger of the corruption itself remains unproven (@jirathip-k notes a 0s-drain gateway restart mid-WAL-write as the likely candidate on the reporting host). That's a separate question from this PR, which bounds the amplification regardless of what damages the file. Closes #88224

signal.title: feat(desktop): remember the Quick Entry target picker choice
signal.text: ## What The Quick Entry composer's session-target picker (Current chat / New session / a recent session) reset to **Current chat** on every summon, with no way to change that default. Users whose habit is firing prompts into a new session had to re-pick the target every single time. This PR persists the user's last picker choice in localStorage, so a summon opens on the same target they chose before — while the shipped default (current chat) stays untouched for everyone who never touches the picker. ## Why this shape - Default preserved: the initial state and the dismiss/shown reset still fall back to `QUICK_TARGET_CURRENT` when nothing was persisted. - Reducer stays pure: `dismiss`/`shown` accept an optional `resetTarget`, the window layer injects the persisted preference. Omitted field = exactly the old behavior. - Storage is renderer-local (like the picker options themselves); the main-process `quick-entry.json` (`enabled`/`shortcut`) is untouched. ## Changes - `apps/desktop/src/store/quick-entry.ts` — `QUICK_ENTRY_TARGET_STORAGE_KEY`, `loadPersistedQuickEntryTarget`/`persistQuickEntryTarget` (safe fallbacks), `createInitialQuickComposerState()`, optional `resetTarget` on dismiss/shown events. - `apps/desktop/src/app/quick-entry/quick-entry-app.tsx` — seed the composer with the persisted target, persist on picker change, reset to the preference on summon. - `apps/desktop/src/store/quick-entry.test.ts` — 6 new tests (persisted load, garbage fallback, persist round-trip, re-summon honoring the preference, default preserved). ## Verification - `vitest run src/store/quick-entry.test.ts` → 23 passed (17 existing + 6 new). - Renderer rebuild verified the new key lands in `dist/assets/quick-entry-*.js`.

signal.title: [Bug]: API server GET /health ignores API_SERVER_KEY while other routes require it
signal.text: ### Bug Description When the API server is enabled **and** `API_SERVER_KEY` is set, `GET /health` still returns HTTP 200 **without** an `Authorization` header. Other OpenAI-compatible routes on the same listener (`GET /v1/models`, `POST /v1/chat/completions`) correctly reject missing/invalid bearers with HTTP 401 (`gateway_auth_error`). Docs say `API_SERVER_KEY` is required for every deployment, including loopback. The unauthenticated `/health` route contradicts that and makes it easy for clients (and status checks) to think “the API is open” when chat is actually gated. `GET /health/detailed` **does** call `_check_auth`. The simple `/health` handler does not. Observed on Hermes Agent v0.20.2. Confirmed by reading `gateway/platforms/api_server.py` (`_handle_health` vs `_handle_health_detailed`). Intentionally **not** attaching `hermes debug share` output — it would include host identity, config, and logs. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Enable the API server with a non-placeholder `API_SERVER_KEY` (loopback bind is enough). 2. Start the gateway so the API server is listening on the default loopback port. 3. `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8642/health` (no Authorization) 4. `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8642/v1/models` (no Authorization) 5. Repeat step 4 with `Authorization: Bearer $API_SERVER_KEY`. ### Expected Behavior Either: - `GET /health` requires the same bearer as `/v1/models` and `/v1/chat/completions`, **or** - docs explicitly mark `/health` as a public liveness probe (and clients such as the Raycast “API Server Status” command should not treat an unauthenticated 200 as “fully configured”). ### Actual Behavior - `GET /health` with no Authorization → HTTP 200 `{"status":"ok",...}` - `GET /v1/models` / `POST /v1/chat/completions` with no Authorization → HTTP 401 - `GET /health/detailed` requires the bearer ### Affected Component - Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp) - Other (API server / OpenAI-compatible HTTP) ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) - N/A (CLI only) ### Debug Report Omitted on purpose (privacy). Reproduction is the curl sequence above against a stock loopback API server. ### Operating System macOS ### Python Version 3.11.x ### Hermes Version 0.20.2

signal.title: fix(nous): honor "thinking off" on Portal models that can honor it
signal.text: Turning thinking off did nothing on the Nous Portal. The profile refused to send `reasoning: {enabled: false}` for any model, and sending nothing means the *upstream* default applies — which on a thinking-first route like `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` is thinking ON. Users who disabled thinking kept paying for it on every turn. Reported against a real session: `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` via `nous` with `reasoning_config: {"enabled": false}`, 2,193 reasoning tokens against 3,766 output tokens. ## What the Portal actually accepts Probed live against `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4-flash`, and `arcee-ai/trinity-large-thinking` (reasoning tokens on an identical prompt): | sent | v4-pro | v4-flash | trinity | |---|---|---|---| | nothing (previous behavior) | 1500 | 204 | 1342 | | `extra_body.thinking: {type: disabled}` | 525 | 1194 | 1266 | | `reasoning: {enabled: false}` | **0** | **0** | HTTP 400 | `reasoning: {enabled: false}` is the only shape that works. DeepSeek's own `extra_body.thinking` is not forwarded upstream by the Portal, so the direct-DeepSeek translation is not an option on this route. The blanket omission was over-broad rather than wrong: the Portal rejects a disable only on **reasoning-mandatory** routes, with `Reasoning is mandatory for this model`. Its catalog flags those per model (`reasoning.mandatory`), so that flag now gates the omission instead of the model list being empty. Independently corroborated by #70058, where the Portal's parameter-validation 400 enumerates the efforts it accepts as `"max"|"xhigh"|"high"|"medium"|"low"|"minimal"|"none"` — a disable has been in the accepted set all along. ## How The Portal serves OpenRouter's catalog schema, so `parse_openrouter_reasoning_capabilities` and the existing cache-only tri-state contract carry over unchanged. Only the HTTP fetch is generalized across the two catalogs; each keeps its own cache since they list different models. The Portal 403s a catalog read with no User-Agent, so the shared fetch sends one. A model the catalog can't speak to — cold cache, unlisted route, catalog unreachable — keeps the old omit-everything behavior. A silently-ignored disable is a much better failure than a 400 that kills the turn. ## Verification End-to-end against the live Portal, with `{"enabled": false}` and the fix in place: ``` deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro reasoning_tokens=0 (was 1500) deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash reasoning_tokens=0 (was 204) arcee-ai/trinity-large-thinking reasoning_tokens=3956 no 400 ``` Two stale tests encoded the old premise (`Nous rejects enabled=false`) and are corrected. New coverage pins the profile's wire shape per catalog verdict and the Portal capability lookup, both offline.
signal.author: OutThisLife

signal.title: fix(desktop): let sessions in Home be moved into a freshly created project
signal.text: # fix(desktop): "Move to project" no longer dead-ends when only the Home bucket exists ## Background Hermes Desktop's sidebar groups sessions by Project. A session whose `cwd` sits inside a folder no explicit project owns falls into the synthetic **Home** bucket (id `__no_project__`, `isNoProject: true`). The kebab menu's **"Move to project"** submenu (`MoveToProjectItems` in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/session-actions-menu.tsx`) shows the projects the session CAN move into — the current owner is excluded, and `isNoProject` is excluded because Home has no folder to re-home into. When the user has not yet created any explicit project, the submenu renders exactly one item: a **disabled** "No other projects" line. There is no path from that disabled line to actually moving the session. The user has to: 1. Close the menu 2. Open the sidebar's "New project" button 3. Re-pick the directory the session is already in 4. Type a project name 5. Confirm 6. Reopen the session's kebab menu → Move to project → pick the new project Six steps to do what should be a two-click operation. The session's existing `cwd` already points at exactly the folder the new project needs. Reproduction is verified live on Hermes Desktop 0.17.0 (macOS arm64). Before this change: sidebar projects view shows only "Home", session kebab → Move to project shows a single disabled item, no move is possible. After this change: the submenu shows an actionable "New project…" entry that completes the move in two clicks. ## Root cause The filter in `MoveToProjectItems`: ```ts const targets = tree.filter(node => node.id !== currentProjectId && !node.isNoProject && // ← Home is always filtered out projectRootCwd(node) ) if (targets.length === 0) { return <kit.Item disabled>{p.moveNoProjects}</kit.Item> // ← dead-end } ``` is correct as far as it goes: Home really has nowhere to move a session INTO. The bug is the **fallback when there is no real target**: instead of exposing the only available action (create a project), the menu tells the user nothing can be done. ## Existing solutions surveyed | Path | What it does | Why it doesn't solve the dead-end | | --- | --- | --- | | Sidebar's `SidebarBlankState` (sidebar/index.tsx:1762) `onNewProject` | One-click project creation from the empty Projects view | Only reachable when the user is already in the empty Projects view AND has no session selected; doesn't fire from the per-session menu | | `openProjectCreate()` (store/projects.ts) | Opens the create dialog with an empty folder list | The dialog requires the user to re-pick the session's cwd AND name the project; no callback fires after creation | | `moveSessionToProject(sessionId, projectId, profile)` (store/projects.ts:526) | Re-anchors a session to a project's root folder via `session.workspace.move` RPC | Requires an existing `projectId`; not useful when no project exists yet | | `ProjectDialog` (app/chat/sidebar/project-dialog.tsx) | Mounted dialog that reads `$projectDialog` atom; handles create / rename / add-folder | Lacked an `onCreated` callback seam and a folder-prefill mechanism, so it couldn't be chained from a submenu | The fix wires together the last two rows: extend `$projectDialog` state with `prefillFolder` and `onCreated`, then have `MoveToProjectItems` call `openProjectCreate({ prefillFolder, onCreated })` instead of the bare `openProjectCreate()`. ## Approach Two minimal, additive changes: 1. `apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts` — `$projectDialog` state gains `prefillFolder?: string` and `onCreated?: (project) => void | Promise<void>` fields. `openProjectCreate(options)` carries them through. 2. `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/project-dialog.tsx` — the `useEffect` that resets state on open now seeds `folders` from `prefillFolder` when `mode === 'create'`. After a successful submit, if `onCreated` is set, it's invoked AFTER the dialog closes (so the user is back in the menu and toasts land against the right surface). Errors in the callback toast but never roll back the project that was just created. 3. `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/session-actions-menu.tsx` — `MoveToProjectItems`: - When `targets.length === 0` (only Home exists): instead of a disabled "No other projects" item, render an actionable "New project…" item that opens the create dialog with the session's cwd prefilled. - When `targets.length > 0`: keep existing behaviour but add a separator + "New project…" entry at the bottom so the affordance is reachable from any session, not only the Home case. - The new entry closes over an `onCreated` callback that calls `moveSessionToProject(sessionId, project.id, profile)` and shows the existing "Moved to …" success toast. What we **preserve**: - `MoveToProjectItems`'s filter logic — the Home exclusion and "current project exclusion" rules are still correct. - `openProjectCreate()`'s RPC contract — `projects.create` body is unchanged. - `moveSessionToProject()`'s RPC contract — `session.workspace.move` is unchanged. What we **do not duplicate**: - A new "move to project" RPC method. - A new project-creation entry point. - A new persisted store for the create dialog's transient state. - Any new IPC surface, env var, or schema field. ## What this preserves about the user's mental model - A session's `cwd` is the most natural anchor for "what project does this belong to". The fix does not change that — it uses the existing `cwd` as the new project's primary folder, exactly as the manual flow does. - "Move" still means `session.workspace.move` (re-anchor cwd + git identity, refresh the live agent). The fix reuses the existing `moveSessionToProject` helper end-to-end. - The Home bucket remains the "no project owner" fallback for backward compatibility — `isNoProject` is still filtered from the target list because Home really has nothing to move into. ## Regression coverage `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/session-actions-menu.test.tsx`: - The pre-existing "opens the dropdown on click without a tooltip on the kebab" test continues to assert rename + archive are reachable (unchanged assertions — the new code path doesn't touch them). - A new test "offers 'New project and move here…' when the sidebar has only the Home bucket" seeds `$projectTree` to a single Home node, opens the menu, drills into the Move-to-project submenu, asserts the new affordance is **enabled** (not disabled), clicks it, and asserts `openProjectCreate` was called with the session's cwd prefilled. The test mocks both `openProjectCreate` and `moveSessionToProject` and verifies the entry point — the dialog driver is covered by its own existing tests (`project-dialog.test.tsx`). Full suite on the upstream/main worktree: ``` Test Files 428 passed (428) Tests 3843 passed (3843) ``` ## Decision rationale - **Why not a separate "create project" sidebar button?** That path exists (`SidebarBlankState.onNewProject`) but it's reachable from the empty-projects view, not from inside a session's kebab menu. Adding a second entry point under every session is the cheapest way to cover the case the user is in when they discover the gap: staring at a session they can't move. - **Why not auto-create a project on first session?** That would be surprising — the user didn't ask for a project to exist. The fix keeps the create step explicit (the user names the project) and just collapses the rest. - **Why callback instead of a hard-coded move in the dialog?** The dialog is reusable; `openProjectCreate()` is also called from the sidebar with no follow-up work. The callback keeps the dialog single-purpose and lets the menu compose the create-then-move without the dialog knowing what "move" means. ## Who should enable this Every Hermes Desktop user who has at least one session in the Home bucket and wants to re-home it into a project. The change is behavioural only — no flag, no opt-in, no new env var. The old behaviour (a disabled "No other projects" line) is replaced wherever the dead-end would otherwise appear. ## Platform compatibility | Platform | Behaviour | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | macOS (Apple Silicon) | Tested live on Hermes 0.17.0 build | Reproduced and verified after fix | | macOS (Intel) | Same | Renderer-only change, no native code path | | Windows | Same | Renderer-only change | | Linux | Same | Renderer-only change | | Web Dashboard / TUI | N/A | The bug exists only in the desktop sidebar's session menu | ## Quick-start guide There is nothing to enable. The change ships with the next Hermes Desktop release. After updating: 1. Open the sidebar, click the **Projects** tab. 2. If only the **Home** bucket is visible, right-click any session row under Home → ⋮ → **Move to project** → **New project…**. 3. The dialog opens with the session's directory prefilled. Type a name → **Create**. 4. The session is re-homed into the new project immediately. A "Moved to …" toast confirms. If the sidebar already has explicit projects, the **New project…** entry also appears at the bottom of the Move-to-project submenu — it's just no longer required to reach the feature. ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Cause | Fix | | --- | --- | --- | | Submenu still shows disabled "No other projects" | Build is older than this PR's merge; desktop loaded a stale `app.asar` | Run `hermes update` (or rebuild + restart the desktop app) and reload the window | | Clicking "New project…" opens a dialog with no folders | Session has no `cwd` recorded (rare — detached sessions) | Pick any folder manually; the move still works because the dialog's folder becomes the new project's root | | "Moved to …" toast fires but the session still appears under Home | The `session.workspace.move` RPC succeeded locally but the sidebar hasn't refreshed | Click the sidebar's **Projects** tab to force a tree refresh; the next `projects.tree` poll will land the new owner | | Clicking the new entry does nothing | Stale build cache for `dist/assets/` | Restart Hermes Desktop — the renderer reloads the new bundle | ## Diff stat ``` apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/project-dialog.tsx | 28 +++- apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/session-actions-menu.test.tsx | 150 ++++++++++++++++++--- apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/session-actions-menu.tsx | 59 +++++++- apps/desktop/src/i18n/en.ts | 1 + apps/desktop/src/i18n/types.ts | 1 + apps/desktop/src/i18n/zh.ts | 1 + apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts | 16 ++- 7 files changed, 228 insertions(+), 28 deletions(-) ```

signal.title: fix(agent): recover inline reasoning stripped by the think scrubber
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #89647: providers that inline reasoning (MiniMax-M3 streams `<think>…</think>` inside content) never send a `reasoning_content` delta, so the desktop reasoning pane stays dead even though reasoning happened. ## Approach - `StreamingThinkScrubber` (agent/think_scrubber.py, #17924) already strips inline think blocks from streamed content but discarded the text. It now **collects** the stripped text (block content, closed pairs, end-of-stream tail) with a `reasoning()` accessor that removes tag markup. - `_relay_final_response` (agent/chat_completion_helpers.py) populates `reasoning_content` from the scrubber when the provider returned no reasoning delta. ## Relation to #43827 / #43836 - This fixes the **structured-field extraction** side of the MiniMax-M3 reasoning family. The English `<think>` blocks are already suppressed from visible output by the scrubber (#17924) — this PR recovers them into `reasoning_content` so the desktop reasoning pane populates. - The **Chinese reasoning tags** (思考/反思/推理/推敲) leak reported in #43827 (still open; #43836 closed without merge) is a separate symptom in the same family: those tags are not in the scrubber's tag set, so they are neither suppressed nor collected here. Out of scope for this PR. ## Test Plan - 5 new tests in `TestReasoningCollection` (tests/agent/test_think_scrubber.py): split block across deltas / closed pair in one delta / no-reasoning empty / tag markup stripped / reset clears. - Full file: 25/25 pass. `ruff check` clean. ## Risk / Exclusions - Scrubber behavior for visible output is unchanged (collection only); reasoning() is additive. - Only fills reasoning_content when the provider gave none — native reasoning deltas still take precedence. - No changes to streaming delivery, prompts, the content scrubber, or the Chinese-tag path (#43827). References #89647

signal.title: RFC: per-Bot credential grants — make credential access declared instead of emergent
signal.text: ## Summary Hermes has no first-class notion of a **credential grant** — a declared statement that Bot X may use credential Y. Whether a profile can reach a given secret is instead an emergent side effect of four unrelated mechanisms: 1. which `.env` file happens to hold the value (`<profile>/.env`, seeded empty at create), 2. whether the *shell environment* happens to hold it (fall-through), 3. whether someone symlinked `auth.json` between profiles (the pattern #19436 asks to bless), 4. whether `agent/secret_scope.py` is enforcing, which today depends on `gateway.multiplex_profiles` being on. Because access is emergent rather than declared, the system fails in **both directions at once**: credentials leak between profiles that should be isolated, *and* there is no supported way to deliberately share one — or to give a Bot its own login for a third-party service. This issue proposes making the grant explicit. It is an RFC: the mechanism below is a starting point, not a settled design. ## Evidence: both failure directions are live **Accidental sharing** — an open cluster, not isolated bugs: - #84079 — platform credentials from the default profile are applied to every profile, causing N-way turn fan-out - #66930 — bare profiles (no `.env`) inherit Matrix credentials from root `~/.hermes/.env` - #87722 — secondary-profile cron delivery escapes secret scope and uses default-profile credentials - #77969 — profile-scoped `.env` load overwrites process-global `os.environ`, clobbering other profiles' adapters - #71143 — cloned profile inherits platform bot tokens; second gateway serves the same bot - #83182, #83391 — cron delivery and the Channels page resolve the wrong bot token under multiplex **No supported deliberate sharing** — #19436 asks for `hermes profile create --link-auth <base>`, and today has to hand-roll `ln -sf` against `auth.json` and rely on `utils.atomic_replace`'s symlink-preserving behavior being load-bearing. That both classes are open simultaneously is the tell: the problem is not a bug in sharing or a bug in isolation, it is the absence of a place to *say which one you meant*. ## Current state (verified) - **Per-profile `.env`, seeded empty.** `create_profile` writes a `.env` at 0600 with the header *"API keys and tokens set here override the shell environment"* ([hermes_cli/profiles.py](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/hermes_cli/profiles.py) — the seeding block). The comment there records exactly this confusion: without the file, *"the profile silently inherited API keys from the shell environment — users reasonably read that as 'the new profile reads the root .env'."* Seeding an empty file makes the file exist; it does not make the fall-through stop. - **`agent/secret_scope.py` already implements the hard part.** It is a fail-closed, context-local, profile-scoped resolver: `set_secret_scope(mapping)` installs the active profile's secrets on a contextvar that propagates into worker threads, and `get_secret(name)` raises rather than falling back to `os.environ` when a scope is missing. **But** the fail-closed behavior is gated on `set_multiplex_active(True)`, which is only called at gateway startup when `gateway.multiplex_profiles` is set. Everywhere else — CLI, TUI, desktop, cron, Bot Mode — it transparently reads `os.environ`. - **`agent/credential_pool.py`** manages same-provider failover across multiple credentials and already reads through `secret_scope`. - **Bot Mode defaults to sharing.** Per the [Bot Mode guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/website/docs/user-guide/bot-mode.md): *"by default the new Bot shares one OAuth/token pool with the main profile, so credential refreshes cannot invalidate each other."* Sensible for provider keys; wrong as a universal default for third-party service logins. So the enforcement primitive exists and is good. What is missing is (a) a declared grant model to enforce *against*, and (b) enforcement outside the multiplex gateway. ## Why this matters beyond the bug cluster The industry model this is converging on is per-agent, incrementally granted access. xAI's [Grok Bot](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/overview) (launched 2026-08-11) frames setup as *"Create a Bot, message it, and grant access as needed"* — each Bot holds **its own logins** and its own browser sessions, and capability accrues through use rather than being configured up front. Hermes' Bot Mode is already close on the social model (persistent Bots, Bot Chat, group chats, routines, bot-to-bot messaging). Credentials are the axis where it is furthest away: a Hermes Bot cannot hold its own account for a service, and the default is to share the operator's pool. Closing this is worth more toward "a roster of specialists you actually trust with work" than any further creation-UX polish. ## Proposal (RFC) **1. Declare grants per profile.** A `credentials:` block in the profile's own config, naming what this Bot may resolve and where it comes from: ```yaml credentials: # Share the operator's pool — today's Bot Mode default, now explicit. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: { from: default } XAI_API_KEY: { from: default } # This Bot's own login. Lives in <profile>/.env, never resolved by others. GITHUB_TOKEN: { from: self } # Explicitly borrowed from a named profile (the supported form of #19436). SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: { from: profile, name: comms-bot } ``` with **deny-by-default**: a name not listed does not resolve, and never falls through to `os.environ` or the root `.env`. **2. Make `secret_scope` the universal enforcement point.** Decouple fail-closed behavior from `gateway.multiplex_profiles` and drive it from whether the active profile declares a `credentials:` block. Profiles without one keep exactly today's behavior, so this is opt-in and back-compatible; profiles with one get deny-by-default everywhere — CLI, TUI, desktop, cron, and gateway alike. This is a smaller change than it sounds because the call sites already route through `get_secret`. **3. Grant incrementally, in conversation.** The Grok-like half. When a Bot hits an ungranted name, the fail-closed raise should surface as a *request* — "this Bot needs `GITHUB_TOKEN`; grant from the shared pool, or add its own?" — resolved by the operator and written back to the grant block. This is the piece that makes per-Bot credentials usable rather than a config chore. **4. Retire the symlink pattern** by making `{ from: profile, name: ... }` the blessed form, closing #19436 without every downstream tool reinventing `ln -sf`. ## Open questions - **Where do grants live?** A `credentials:` block in `config.yaml` is discoverable but puts an access-control policy in a file the agent can edit — note #79030 (shell bypasses `patch`/`write_file` guardrails on sensitive config) and #70942 (`auth.json` missing from write-denied paths). A separate `grants.yaml` on the write-denied list may be safer. - **Migration.** Every existing profile behaves as `from: default` for everything. Is opt-in-per-profile enough, or does this need a `hermes profile grants audit` to show what each profile *currently* resolves before anyone flips it? - **Interaction with `credential_pool`.** Pool failover across several keys for one provider needs the grant to name a pool, not a single variable. - **Does `from: default` deserve to stay the Bot Mode default?** It is right for provider keys and wrong for service logins. Possibly the default should be per-key-class rather than global. - **Scope of enforcement.** Subprocesses spawned with `env=dict(os.environ)` are the classic leak path (#77969). Deny-by-default is only real if the spawn path is scrubbed too — that may be the largest slice of the work. ## Related - #19436 — native auth-sharing across forked profiles (the deliberate-sharing half) - #84079, #66930, #87722, #77969, #71143, #83182, #83391 — the accidental-sharing cluster - #21574 — per-user agent isolation and identity-based permissions - #78802 — principal-to-profile authorization for multiplexed gateways - #79030, #70942 — sensitive-config write guardrails, relevant to where grants are stored - #90319 / #90331 — agent-callable profile creation; a Bot created by an agent should be grantable the same way

signal.title: feat(mcp): bridge MCP ImageContent to auxiliary vision summaries for text-only models
signal.text: ## Summary MCP tools that return `ImageContent` blocks (browser screenshots, `read_image`, `read_video` frames) are effectively **blind for pure-text main models**. Hermes caches the image bytes and hands the model only a bare `MEDIA:<path>` tag — for a text-only provider that tag carries zero pixel information. This PR adds a **fail-open, config-gated bridge**: after an MCP image block is cached, if the user has configured `auxiliary.vision`, the image is described once by the auxiliary vision model and the text summary is appended alongside the `MEDIA:` tag (dual-track output). Text-only models go from "cannot see the image at all" to "sees a full description". ```text MCP tool ──ImageContent──▶ Hermes mcp_tool result pipeline │ ├─▶ MEDIA:<path> (unchanged, rendering) └─▶ [图片内容摘要] <summary> (NEW: aux vision bridge) ``` ## Problem `tools/mcp_tool.py` handles MCP `ImageContent` by caching bytes via `cache_image_from_bytes` and returning `MEDIA:<path>` (this exact behavior is confirmed by Qwen-MM-Plugins' official Hermes manual: "provider receives no image pixels"). For vision-capable main models this is fine; for text-only models the information is lost. The built-in `vision_analyze` tool exists as a manual fallback, but requires the model to *remember* it is blind and explicitly invoke a second tool — an automatic bridge removes that failure mode. ## Solution New `_summarize_mcp_image(image_tag)` in `tools/mcp_tool.py`, invoked from the existing image-block branch of the MCP tool-result loop: - **Fail-open contract**: any failure / timeout / misconfiguration returns `""`; the original `MEDIA:` tag always survives. A single bad block never kills a tool result (matches the file's existing fail-open conventions). - **Config gate**: no `auxiliary.vision` configured → complete no-op (zero footprint). `auxiliary.vision.summarize_mcp_images: false` explicitly disables. - **Timeout**: per-image cap `auxiliary.vision.mcp_summary_timeout` (default 20s) so a slow vision backend cannot wedge the MCP tool result. - **Session dedupe**: image cache paths are content hashes, so the same image is analyzed at most once per process (`_MCP_IMAGE_SUMMARY_CACHE`). - **Model alignment**: resolves `auxiliary.vision.model` exactly like the built-in `vision_analyze` tool (`config model → AUXILIARY_VISION_MODEL env → None`), avoiding the `provider=auto` fallback error that occurs when no cloud vision is configured. Narrow-waist: zero new core tools, zero new env vars, no system-prompt changes, no prompt-cache invalidation. Only the MCP result-rendering edge changes. ## Comparison | Option | Info available to text model | Latency | Change size | |---|---|---|---| | Status quo | 0% (path only) | 0 | 0 | | **This PR** | 100% (path + summary) | 5-72s (local vision model) | +100 lines | | Manual vision_analyze | 100% | same | 0 (model must remember) | | Switch to multimodal main model | 100% native | 0 | large | ## Real-machine validation (macOS M5 Max, Mage-VL-8bit local + deepseek-v4-flash text model) 9 scenarios, controlled comparison (same model, same prompt, only the input differs): - **Text information gain**: 66–76 chars (size metadata only) → 1,263–2,073 chars (visual description) = **18–27×** - **Reasoning capability**: K-line chart ID, financial OCR extraction, webpage recognition all went **0% → 100%** correct answers with the bridge; 3/3 "cannot answer" without it - Video frames summarized accurately (5.3s/frame); PDF via `visualize` already returns extracted text (bridge correctly not triggered) - Documented failure modes: vision hallucination on low-information images (1×1 px red dot → invented "travel webpage"), prompt-dependence of vision output (captcha read correctly with targeted prompt, hallucinated with generic prompt) ## Security audit **SECURITY-AUDIT.md (summary)** - **Threat model**: image content becomes model-readable text → new prompt-injection carrier (malicious text embedded in an image gets transcribed into the summary). - **Mitigations**: summary is explicitly tagged `[图片内容摘要]` (data marker, not instruction); the bridge only *describes*, never executes; per-user opt-out via `summarize_mcp_images: false`; timeout bounds resource use; session cache bounds repeat analysis. - **No new credential surface**: reuses the existing `auxiliary.vision` config and the existing `vision_analyze_tool` path (which already handles local-file confinement via the single resolver). MCP subprocess env filtering (`_build_safe_env`) unchanged. - **No new env vars**: config.yaml only, per Hermes convention. - **No telemetry / no outbound beyond the already-configured aux vision endpoint.** **SECURITY-BASELINE.md (summary)** - Default configuration = test baseline: with no `auxiliary.vision` the bridge is a complete no-op (verified by test `test_no_vision_config_is_noop`). - All escape hatches verified on real path, not mocks: unit contract tests (7) + real integration through the full MCP handler pipeline against a live local vision model + 120 existing MCP tests pass unchanged. **DECISION-RECORD.md (summary)** - Alternative A (feed native image blocks to text providers) rejected: violates narrow-waist, high blast radius. - Alternative B (this PR): edge-only change, fail-open, reversible via config. - 100-line patch chosen deliberately — the expensive parts (vision understanding, caching, routing) already exist in Hermes; only the automatic trigger point was missing. ## Who should enable - Users running **text-only main models** who connect MCP servers that return images (screenshots, charts, `read_image`, `read_video`) and who have any `auxiliary.vision` model configured (local or cloud, OpenAI-compatible). - Users who already call `vision_analyze` manually for MCP images — the bridge automates exactly that step. - Users of vision-capable main models: no change (MEDIA tag already works; summary is extra text, harmless). ## Platform compatibility - macOS / Linux: full support (asyncio + stdlib only). - Windows: bridge is POSIX-agnostic; the existing MCP pipeline's platform guards apply unchanged. ## Quick start ```yaml # ~/.hermes/config.yaml auxiliary: vision: provider: custom:mlx # or any OpenAI-compatible vision endpoint model: /path/to/your-vlm base_url: http://localhost:8123/v1 api_key: '' summarize_mcp_images: true # default true once auxiliary.vision exists mcp_summary_timeout: 30 # default 20s; raise for large/complex images ``` Restart Hermes. Any MCP tool that returns an image will now include a `[图片内容摘要]` text block next to the `MEDIA:` tag. ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Cause | Fix | |---|---|---| | No summary appears | No `auxiliary.vision` configured | Add the config block above | | Summary times out on large images | 20s default too tight for 100KB+ images | Raise `mcp_summary_timeout` | | `No LLM provider configured for task=vision` | `model` missing from `auxiliary.vision` | Set `model:` (mirrors built-in vision_analyze) | | Don't want summaries | Opt-out | `summarize_mcp_images: false` | | Vision model hallucinates on captcha/abstract images | Low-information image + generic prompt | Use targeted prompts per tool type (future work); keep human review for critical data | ## Tests - `tests/tools/test_mcp_image_summary.py`: 7 new tests (no-op without config, opt-out, success path, session cache, failure fail-open ×3 variants, timeout fail-open, non-image/missing-file no-op) - Existing MCP suites pass: `test_mcp_image_content.py`, `test_mcp_resource_content.py`, `test_mcp_tool.py` (124 passed total incl. new tests)
